chunks.title: Childcare Subsidy
chunks.text: Childcare Subsidy is a payment that helps families with the cost of pre-school childcare.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may get a Childcare Subsidy if: - you're the principal caregiver of a dependent child - you're a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident - your family is on a low or middle income. Principal caregiver You should also normally live in New Zealand and intend to stay here. The child must be: - aged either: under 5, or over 5 if they're going to a cohort entry school (where new entrants start together on a set date after they turn 5), or under 6 if you get a Child Disability Allowance for them - under 5, or - over 5 if they're going to a cohort entry school (where new entrants start together on a set date after they turn 5), or - under 6 if you get a Child Disability Allowance for them - attending an approved early childhood education programme or service for 3 or more hours a week.

chunks.title: Approved programmes
chunks.text: Approved programmes include licensed early childhood education and care services, eg: - kindergartens and preschools - childcare centres and creches - playcentres and playgroups - Kohanga Reo, Punanga Reo, Aoga and other programmes with a language and culture focus - approved home-based care.

chunks.title: Check if you can get Childcare Subsidy
chunks.text: To find out if you could get Childcare Subsidy and what else you might qualify for, use our 'Check what you might get' tool.

chunks.title: Hours paid for
chunks.text: A Childcare Subsidy is normally paid for up to 9 hours of childcare a week if you're not working, studying or training. You may be able to get up to 50 hours a week if you're in one of these situations: - working, studying or on an approved training course - involved in an activity that Work and Income has asked you to do - a shift worker who works nights - seriously ill or disabled - caring for a child in hospital or for a child you get the Child Disability Allowance for. In most cases you can't get the Childcare Subsidy for more than 9 hours a week if the child's other parent or caregiver can care for them.

chunks.title: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education
chunks.text: You can only get Childcare Subsidy for the same hours you're getting 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (ECE) if: - your child is at a home-based educator, and - the home-based educator is charging a top up payment for the same hours as 20 Hours ECE. Home-based educators may charge you a top up payment to cover the difference between their normal hourly rate and 20 Hours ECE. 20 Hours ECE (Ministry of Education)external

chunks.title: Public holidays
chunks.text: We pay Childcare Subsidy for public holidays like Waitangi Day and anniversary days. However, most programmes close between Christmas and New Year, so payments won’t be made during this time.

chunks.title: Optional charges and donations
chunks.text: You can’t get Childcare Subsidy for optional charges and donations requested by your childcare provider.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: How much you get depends on: - the size of your family - your income - how many hours a week your child goes to the childcare provider, and - the amount and type of childcare fee. Childcare assistance starts from the date the care starts (or from the date you apply if you apply after it starts). All subsidies are paid directly to the childcare provider. View our current ratesexternal

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: We suggest you apply at least 3 to 4 weeks before you need your subsidy to start. We can grant you the financial assistance you're entitled to from the date you first contact us, or the date your childcare started, whichever is later, if you complete your application within 20 working days of that date. If you're a Youth Service client, you need to talk to your Youth Service provider. How you apply depends on whether you're applying for Childcare Subsidy only or other payments as well.

chunks.title: Applying for Childcare Subsidy only
chunks.text: What form you fill out depends on whether you're an existing client of ours or a new client.

chunks.title: Existing client
chunks.text: If you already get payments from us, you can apply online using the SmartStart website. You'll need your: - RealMe login - if you haven't registered for RealMe, you'll be asked to register in SmartStart - income details - partner's income details - dependent children’s birth certificates - Work and Income client number - IRD number - email address, so SmartStart can send you notifications during the application process. If your (or your partner's) information has changed, you'll also need to provide proof of your identity. You can upload your documents through SmartStart when you apply. Apply online (SmartStart)external Register for RealMe (Department of Internal Affairs)external

chunks.title: New client
chunks.text: If you don't get any payments from us, you and your partner (if you have one) need to complete the Childcare Assistance application form. Your childcare provider also needs to complete the supervisor's section inside this form. You can either: - email the application form, and any other documents we've asked you to get, to Centralised_childcare_reviews@msd.govt.nz, or - ask your childcare provider to send this to us on your behalf. If you can't print the form out, you can call us to get an application form sent to you, or pick one up from your nearest service centre. You can bring the completed form into a service centre. Find your nearest service centre If you can’t bring the form into a service centre, call us to find out how to get it to us.

chunks.title: New client
chunks.text: Phone us If this is your first time applying for a benefit or ongoing payment, you need to bring your original government-issued ID into a service centre so we can check it. Checking ID in person helps us make sure we give support to the right person and protect your identity. Verify your identity at a service centre

chunks.title: Applying for Childcare Subsidy and other payments
chunks.text: You can apply online: Apply Online Once you've applied online, we'll tell you what you need to do. This will include having to get your childcare provider to complete the supervisor's section of the Childcare Assistance application form.

chunks.title: Reviews and changes
chunks.text: Childcare assistance is reviewed regularly. It also usually stops or is reviewed: - the day after your job or course ends - after 12 weeks if you stop work because you have a health condition or are injured - when your child reaches the age limit for the subsidy - when your child leaves the pre-school facility or Out of School Care and Recreation (OSCAR) programme - if the child leaves your care. You must also tell us straight away about any changes in your circumstances that could affect your payments, eg: - if you or your partner's income changes - if your child stops going or moves to another early childhood education programme or OSCAR programme - if there's a change in your child's attendance - if the number of hours you (or your partner) work or study each week changes

chunks.title: Reviews and changes
chunks.text: - if the reason why you get a subsidy changes, eg your health improves or your child leaves hospital - your child starts or stops receiving 20 Hours ECE - your home-based educator starts to charge a top up payment for the time your child is getting 20 Hours ECE. Manage your childcare payments

chunks.title: Childcare and OSCAR subsidy obligations
chunks.text: There are things you and your partner need to do when you're getting a Childcare subsidy or Out of school care and recreation (OSCAR) subsidy. If you don't do them, your payment could reduce or stop.

chunks.title: Tell us if something changes
chunks.text: You and your partner must tell us (or your Youth Service Provider if you have one assigned to you) immediately if you: - have a change in work situation, e.g. starting part-time, casual or full-time work (paid or unpaid) - become self-employed or start a business - have changes to your income or financial circumstances - have a boarder or renter that moves in or out, or the payments you get from them change - plan to travel overseas - start or finish study - part-time or full-time - have changes to your personal details, e.g: name address bank account number - name - address - bank account number - have changes to your living situation, e.g: marriage or separation starting or ending a civil union starting or ending a de facto relationship change in the number of children you support

chunks.title: Tell us if something changes
chunks.text: - marriage or separation - starting or ending a civil union - starting or ending a de facto relationship - change in the number of children you support - have a change in accommodation costs - are imprisoned or held in custody on remand - are admitted to or discharged from hospital - are granted an overseas pension - have any other change that may affect your entitlement or rate.

chunks.title: If you don't meet your obligations
chunks.text: If there's any reason why you or your partner can't meet your obligations, talk to us straight away. Contact us If you or your partner don't tell us about changes in your life that might affect your payment entitlement, or rate, then: - your payment may be reviewed and cancelled - you may have to pay back the total amount of any overpayment that you've received - we may impose a penalty (up to 3 times the value of the overpayment) - you may be prosecuted and fined and/or imprisoned.

chunks.title: Going overseas
chunks.text: If you or your partner intend to travel overseas and don't let us know before you leave New Zealand, your payment will be stopped the day after you leave New Zealand.

chunks.title: Civil Defence Payment
chunks.text: When there's an emergency event (e.g. flooding or an earthquake), we may make Civil Defence Payments available. If you've been affected and these payments are available, you may be able to get one. Civil Defence Payments are not currently available. If you’re struggling to meet your essential costs, we may still be able to help with living expenses. Help with living expenses

chunks.title: What the payments cover
chunks.text: Civil Defence Payments can help cover the costs of: - Food - Bedding - Clothing - Accommodation - Loss of income.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You don't have to be on a benefit to qualify for a Civil Defence Payment. You also don't have to be a New Zealand resident. In most cases, it doesn't matter what your income is or what assets you have. You may be able to get a Civil Defence Payment if: - Civil Defence Payments have been made available for an emergency event, and - you don't have insurance to cover your costs. You must also be in one of these situations: - you had to leave your home (e.g. you've been evacuated or you're on stand-by) and can't return - you were away from your home at the time of the emergency and can't return - you must stay in your home, or - you can't work and you've lost income because either: you can't get to work your workplace is closed, or you need to stay with your family or whānau, e.g. to care for a child because their school is closed.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: - you can't get to work - your workplace is closed, or - you need to stay with your family or whānau, e.g. to care for a child because their school is closed. We can't help with accommodation costs if you've been offered free accommodation but choose not to take it. You also can't get a Civil Defence Payment to help pay for Temporary Accommodation Service.

chunks.title: Insurance
chunks.text: If you're not sure whether insurance will cover your costs, or your claim is delayed, you may still qualify for a Civil Defence Payment. However if you get a Civil Defence Payment and then your insurance pays for any costs covered by this, you'll need to pay us back.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: Civil Defence Payments are not currently available. When they are available, this page will be updated with details of who can get it and how to apply.

chunks.title: What you need to tell us
chunks.text: When you apply you'll need to tell us your: - full name - date of birth - phone number - client number (if you have one) - normal home address - current address (if you've had to evacuate your home).

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: How much you can get depends on your circumstances. You can apply for help with more than one type of cost.

chunks.title: Staying in temporary accommodation
chunks.text: If you're staying in temporary accommodation, e.g. hotel or motel, we may be able to pay for your accommodation costs. We'll pay this to your accommodation supplier. If you are: Maximum weekly payment Maximum daily payment Single $1,426 $203.71 A couple, without children $1,504 $214.86 A couple, or sole parent, with children $1,773 $253.29

chunks.title: Staying in hosted accommodation
chunks.text: If you're staying in hosted or billeted accommodation, for example with friends or family or in another private home, we may be able to pay for your accommodation costs. If you are: Maximum weekly payment Maximum daily payment Single $261 $37.29 Sole parent $261, plus $130.50 for each dependent child $37.29, plus $18.64 for each dependent child A couple, without children $438 $62.57 A couple, with children $438, plus $130.50 for each dependent child $62.57, plus $18.64 for each dependent child

chunks.title: You need help with food, bedding or clothing
chunks.text: How much you get depends on your situation. We'll make this payment to you or the supplier, depending on your circumstances. If you are: Maximum amount available Single $400 A couple $600 A couple or sole parent, with 1-2 children $900 A couple or sole parent, with 3+ children $1,110

chunks.title: You've lost income because you can't work
chunks.text: How much you get depends on whether you're staying in hosted or billeted accommodation (e.g. with friends or family), or in a hotel or motel. We'll make this payment directly to you.

chunks.title: After you've applied
chunks.text: We'll call you back within 2 working days to discuss your application, and how it will be paid if it's granted. If you're applying because you've lost income we may also need to contact your employer about your application.

chunks.title: How it's paid
chunks.text: We'll pay the Civil Defence Payment either to you or to your supplier, depending on what you need help with. If you're applying because you: We'll pay the Civil Defence Payment to: Need to replace food, bedding or clothing A Work and Income payment card (green card), usually. Then you can use the card to pay the supplier or shop. In some circumstances we can pay this direct to you. Had to leave your home Your accommodation supplier or host, usually. They'll need to be registered with us as a supplier to receive this. Register as a Work and Income supplier In some circumstances we can pay this directly to you. For example, if your accommodation supplier can't register with us due to the emergency. Lost income

chunks.title: Civilian Amputee Assistance
chunks.text: Civilian Amputee Assistance helps amputees, or those born without a limb(s), with some of their costs when they need to go to an Artificial Limb Centre.

chunks.title: What you can claim
chunks.text: You can claim: - travel costs including public transport, taxi fares (where public transport can't be used), private cars or air fares, depending on your circumstances - costs of meals during travel times or overnight stays - accommodation costs if your appointment times or the distance travelled mean that you have to stay overnight - loss of earnings if you have no sick leave left. If you are aged under 15 or can't travel by yourself you can also claim the costs of someone going with you. You can claim for their travel, accommodation and meals but not for their loss of earnings. You can only claim for costs that can't be met by District Health Boards or any other funding scheme. Generally, the District Health Boards will cover initial artificial limb fitting travel costs if you're still in hospital.

chunks.title: What you can claim
chunks.text: If you've lost a limb due to an accident you can get compensation. Contact ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) about this. Contact ACCexternal

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may get Civilian Amputee Assistance if you need to go to an Artificial Limb Centre to have an artificial limb fitted, adjusted or repaired.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: This depends on your circumstances and the costs you claim.

chunks.title: 1. Fill out a form
chunks.text: Complete the Civilian Amputee Assistance form.

chunks.title: 2. Provide proof
chunks.text: If you're applying before you go to a Limb Centre, you'll need to provide evidence of your appointment and your costs. If the amount you were paid in advance did not meet all your costs, or you chose not to be paid before your appointment, you can apply to have these costs reimbursed. You'll need to: - claim your costs within 6 months of going to the Limb Centre, and - provide evidence of attending the Limb Centre - provide receipts for your costs. If you're claiming for loss of earnings you must provide confirmation of this from your employer. We can grant you the financial assistance you're entitled to from the date you first contact us if you complete your application within 20 working days of that date.

chunks.title: If you're applying for the first time
chunks.text: You need to call us on 0800 559 009 We'll talk with you to understand your situation and how we can help. We'll let you know what information you need to provide and how to get this to us.

chunks.title: If you've applied before
chunks.text: You can post your form and documents to us. Find a service centre

chunks.text: We know there's a lot to sort out when someone passes away. We need to know so we can review their payments, and we may be able to help with other things, like a Funeral Grant.

We'll also send a Funeral Grant application form to this person's partner. If they were single, we'll send this application form to you.

chunks.title: Clothing Allowance for Orphan's Benefit and Unsupported Child's Benefit
chunks.text: A Clothing Allowance is a weekly payment we give you if you get Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for children in your care, to help you pay for their clothing.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You will get a Clothing Allowance if you get Unsupported Child's Benefit or Orphan's Benefit.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: How much you get is based on the age of the child you care for. We'll change the payment automatically when the child's age changes - you don't have to tell us. Clothing allowance payment ratesexternal

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You don't need to apply. You'll get this payment automatically when you get Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit.

chunks.title: Payments
chunks.text: The Clothing Allowance will be paid with your Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit. If this benefit stops, your allowance will also stop.

chunks.title: Childcare Subsidy and cohort entry schools
chunks.text: If you're getting Childcare Subsidy and your child will be going to a cohort entry school, you need to tell us what date they start A cohort entry school is a school where all new entrants start together on a set date after they turn 5. This could be at the beginning of the term or on the mid-term date. If you're not sure when new entrants start at your child's school, check with the school.

chunks.title: Child is not going to a cohort entry school
chunks.text: You don't need to do anything. Your Childcare Subsidy will be paid up until your child turns 5. If they can't start school straight away, we may be able to pay for an extra 4 weeks of childcare. Extending childcare when your child turns 5

chunks.title: Child is going to a cohort entry school
chunks.text: You need to complete the 'Cohort entry school start date' form to tell us what date your child starts school. This is so we can keep paying your Childcare Subsidy until they start.

chunks.title: What you'll need
chunks.text: You'll need the following information to complete this form: - your: client number (you can find this on your Community Services Card or on letters you've received from us) full name date of birth contact number - client number (you can find this on your Community Services Card or on letters you've received from us) - full name - date of birth - contact number - for the child turning 5 who you're getting Childcare Subsidy for: full name date of birth name and location of school school start date. - full name - date of birth - name and location of school - school start date. You can enter details for up to 4 children using this form. We may contact you if we need more information. If a child has left your care, don't complete the form for them, please call us.

chunks.title: What you'll need
chunks.text: Call us Make sure you read all the instructions on the form. Cohort entry school start dateexternal

chunks.title: Have any questions or made a mistake?
chunks.text: Call us if you: - have any questions think you've made a mistake on a form you've submitted have had a change of circumstances since you completed the form. - have any questions - think you've made a mistake on a form you've submitted - have had a change of circumstances since you completed the form. Phone us

chunks.title: Getting Child Disability Allowance
chunks.text: If you get Child Disability Allowance for your child and they're not starting school yet, please call us. We may be able to keep paying your Childcare Subsidy until they start school - until they turn 6.

chunks.title: Community Costs
chunks.text: Community Costs is a weekly payment which helps people in a short-term residential treatment programme meet their essential ongoing costs in the community.

chunks.title: What Community Costs can help with
chunks.text: Community Costs aim to help make it easier for people to go back into the community at the end of their treatment and can help pay for essential costs such as: - accommodation - childcare - storage - hire purchases for essential items. These payments are not for the expenses people might have during the treatment programme.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may get Community Costs if you: - are aged 16 years or more - have ongoing costs in the community that are essential - have no other way of meeting these costs - are in a short-term residential treatment programme (less than 39 weeks). It also depends on: - how much you and your spouse or partner earn - any money or assets you and your spouse or partner have. You must also: - be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident - have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years at any one time since becoming a New Zealand citizen or resident (unless you are a refugee). You should also normally live in New Zealand and intend to stay here.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: How much you get depends on your circumstances and the costs you claim. It also depends on how much you and your partner earn and any money or assets you have. You need to show that you have done everything you can to meet your ongoing essential costs before the Community Costs Payment can be approved.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: Contact the Residential Subsidy Unit on 0800 999 779 to talk about your circumstances.

chunks.title: Community Job Coaching
chunks.text: A job coach can help you prepare for and find work. This is for 18 to 24 year olds in some regions, who have been getting Jobseeker Support for at least 3 months.

chunks.title: How it works
chunks.text: You may be referred to a community provider for job coaching. Your job coach will support you for up to 26 weeks (6 months). They'll help you create a personalised plan to overcome any barriers to employment and help you find a job that suits you. The plan includes activities you need to complete as part of your benefit obligations. If you are referred to Community Job Coaching you must work with them as part of your obligation to find or prepare for work. After you start work, your job coach will keep supporting you for up to 1 year while you settle into your new role.

chunks.title: Bonus payment
chunks.text: There is a bonus payment for some people doing Community Job Coaching who get a job and stay off benefit for 1 year. These people can check if they are eligible and apply for this from October 2026.

chunks.title: Who it is for
chunks.text: You may be asked to do Community Job Coaching if you: - are 18-24 years old - have been getting Jobseeker Support for 3 months or more - live in Auckland, Waikato, Bay of Plenty, East Coast, Wellington, Canterbury or Southern regions.

chunks.title: How to join
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 to book an appointment with a case manager. At the appointment we'll check if you're eligible, and find the right provider for you. If you are referred to Community Job Coaching you must work with them as part of your obligation to find or prepare for work.

chunks.title: Community Services Card
chunks.text: The Community Services Card can help you with the costs of health care and public transport. This means you could pay less on some health services, prescriptions and fares for public transport. Always carry your card with you to make it easy to get the benefits. - You don't have to be on a benefit to qualify for the card. - You can also use the card for healthcare services for your dependent children under 18. We administer the Community Services Card on behalf of the Ministry of Health.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may get the Community Services Card if you: - are 16 or over - either: are a New Zealand citizen are a permanent resident, or have, or have applied for, refugee or protection status - are a New Zealand citizen - are a permanent resident, or - have, or have applied for, refugee or protection status - normally live in New Zealand and intend to stay here. If you’re a dependent child, you can only get a Community Services Card, if your parent or caregiver is getting the: Dependent child - Orphans Benefit - Unsupported Child's Benefit, or - Child Disability Allowance. It also depends on how much income you and your partner get. By income, we mean any money, goods and services you or your partner get from any source, such as:

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: - wages or salary - NZ Superannuation - private pensions (if you get NZ Super and a private pension, only half of your private pension is counted as income) - overseas pensions - interest or dividends from investments - Child support - Paid Parental Leave - Working for Families Tax Credits from Inland Revenue - ACC payments - income from rents

chunks.title: Income limits
chunks.text: For families of more than 6, the limit goes up another $12,440 for each extra person. Family: in this table, a family includes either 1 or 2 adults and the dependent children they care for. For example, a family of 2 is made up of 1 adult and 1 dependent child. A family of 3, can be made up of either 1 adult and their 2 dependent children or 2 adults and 1 dependent child.

chunks.title: What the card can help with
chunks.text: The Community Services Card can reduce the cost of: - visits to a health practitioner (e.g. a doctor or nurse) if you're enrolled at their practice (for yourself, and your dependent children aged 14-17) - ACC visits to a general practice if you're injured (you may not need to be enrolled at their practice - it depends on the practice) - subsidised prescriptions - these are free if you have a Community Services Card - partially or unsubsidised prescriptions, or prescriptions from private specialists - fares for public transport including trains, buses and some ferries - fees for after-hours health practitioner visits - glasses for children under 16 - emergency dental care provided by: hospitals, and approved dental contractors (ask the dental provider if they are an approved contractor)

chunks.title: What the card can help with
chunks.text: - hospitals, and - approved dental contractors (ask the dental provider if they are an approved contractor) - travel and accommodation for treatment at a public hospital you've been referred to outside your area: at least 80km away for adults at least 25km for children - at least 80km away for adults - at least 25km for children - home help.

chunks.title: What the card won't cover
chunks.text: If your child is under 14 and visits their health practitioner (for example their doctor) at their enrolled practice, it will usually be free. If the health practitioner has an extra charge, the Community Services Card won't cover it. You'll need to pay for it. If you need a prescription, there may be part-charges or other pharmacy fees to pay. The Community Services Card won't cover this. You'll need to pay for it.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You don't need to apply for a Community Services Card if we automatically send one to you.

chunks.title: Before you start
chunks.text: We'll automatically send you and your partner a card if you're getting one of these benefits or payments from us: - Accommodation Supplement - Emergency Benefit - Jobseeker Support - Residential Care Subsidy (if you have a partner, they'll need to apply for their own card). - Sole Parent Support - Student Allowance, if you don't have a partner's who's working (if you do have a partner who's working, you'll need to apply) - Supported Living Payment - Veterans Pension - Youth Payment, or - Young Parent Payment. We'll also automatically send you and your partner a card if you're living in public housing, i.e. a Kāinga Ora (Housing NZ) house.

chunks.title: Getting a card for a child you support
chunks.text: We'll automatically send you a Community Services Card for a child you support if you're getting: - Orphans Benefit - Unsupported Child's Benefit, or - Child Disability Allowance You can sign the card on the child's behalf.

chunks.title: Step 1 - Fill out an application form
chunks.text: If you don't automatically get a card sent to you, you'll need to apply for one. You can get an application form in any of these ways: - download the application form below - ring us on 0800 999 999 and ask for one - call into a Work and Income service centre - ask a health practitioner, for example your family doctor or pharmacy. Find a service centre If you get Working for Families Tax Credits, you'll be sent an application form automatically.

chunks.title: Step 2 - Gather your documents
chunks.text: You need to provide 2 documents as proof of identity when you apply for a Community Services Card. If you get NZ Super, you don't need to provide proof of identity. What you need to bring when you apply for Community Services Card

chunks.title: Step 3 - Send everything to us
chunks.text: Send your application form and documents to us at the address on the application form. We'll process your application and let you know if we need anything else. We may send you a letter asking you for proof of your income. We'll explain what you need to send. - If you're self-employed, you must send us your latest full set of business accounts and tax summaries. - You can ask your accountant to send us your financial details, but they can't sign the application form for you.

chunks.title: Step 4 - Getting your card
chunks.text: If your application is approved, we'll send you a Community Services Card. On your card is the date it starts and expires. You can continue to use the card until it expires, even if your circumstances change.

chunks.title: Claim back costs you've already paid for
chunks.text: Sometimes your card might start before you get it in the mail. During this time, you may have paid full price for: - after-hours health practitioner visits - prescriptions. If you did, you may be able to claim some of these costs back. To claim them, you need to: - fill out the 'Reimbursement of Health Overcharges Application Form' - gather all your original receipts - send your application form and receipts to:PO Box 5054Lambton QuayWellington If your application is approved, we'll work out how much the Community Services Card would have covered.

chunks.title: Renewing your card
chunks.text: If your card is due to expire, it will need to be renewed. It takes 3 weeks to get a replacement card.

chunks.title: We may automatically send you a replacement card
chunks.text: In some situations, we'll automatically send you and your partner a replacement card before your old one expires. This will happen if you still meet the criteria and you're getting one of these payments from us: - Accommodation Supplement - Emergency Benefit - Jobseeker Support - Residential Care Subsidy (if you have a partner, they'll need to re-apply for their own replacement card) - Sole Parent Support - Student Allowance if you don't have a partner who's working - Supported Living Payment - Veteran's Pension - Youth Payment, or - Young Parent Payment. We'll also automatically send you and your partner a replacement card if you still meet the criteria and: - you've living in public housing, i.e. a Kāinga Ora (Housing NZ) house, or

chunks.title: We may automatically send you a replacement card
chunks.text: - you get Working for Families from Inland Revenue. If you don't automatically get a replacement card, you'll need to re-apply for one.

chunks.title: If you get NZ Super
chunks.text: Your Community Services Card will stop working when your NZ Super is approved. This is because there's been a change in your circumstances (i.e. your income). You'll need to re-apply for a new card. When you reapply, we'll send you a 'combo card'. This 'combo' card is a combination of both your Community Services Card and your SuperGold card. You'll be able to use your 'combo' card for all discounts and subsidies that the 2 cards provides. Your combo card will have the initials 'CSC' on the back, as well as the expiry date. This identifies it as a combo card. When your combo card is due to expire, we'll automatically send you a new one. However, if you get NZ Super and your income is close to the limit for a Community Services Card, we'll send you a renewal application form. You'll need to complete this and return it to us. Then we'll send you a new combo card.

chunks.title: If you get NZ Super
chunks.text: SuperGold Card

chunks.title: How to re-apply for a replacement card
chunks.text: We'll send you a renewal form before your card expires. You need to fill this out and send it back to your nearest service centre. Find a service centre

chunks.title: Didn't get a replacement card or renewal form
chunks.text: If you don't automatically get a replacement card or a renewal form, call us on 0800 999 999

chunks.title: Can't get Community Services Card
chunks.text: If you can't get the Community Services Card, you may be able to get a: - Prescription subsidy (if you and your family have collected 20 subsidised prescription items in a year), or - High Use Health Card (if you visit a health practitioner, for example your doctor, at least 12 times in 12 months for an ongoing health condition). These are both managed by the Ministry of Health. Prescription subsidy (Ministry of Health)external High Use Health Card (Ministry of Health)external

chunks.title: Community Work Experience
chunks.text: Community Work Experience means you need to get a position at a community or voluntary organisation. You need to do at least 5 hours of work a week, for 4 weeks. This can help you build work-related skills and confidence, as well as make valuable connections in your community. You'll continue to get your full benefit payment until you've finished your Community Work Experience. Once you've finished and come to an appointment with a form that the organisation has signed, you'll move back to green.

chunks.title: When we'll put you on Community Work Experience
chunks.text: If you move to orange in the traffic light system, you need to meet with us while you're at orange. At that meeting we may decide to put you on Community Work Experience when you move to red, instead of reducing your benefit. You may be put on Community Work Experience if: - this is the first time in the last 2 years you haven't met your obligations - you don't have a good reason for not meeting your obligations - you meet with us while you're at orange in the traffic light system - you have dependent children or a dedicated case manager. We'll also make sure Community Work Experience is suitable for you. We may not put you on Community Work Experience if, for example: - you're already doing job search activities, or

chunks.title: When we'll put you on Community Work Experience
chunks.text: - you're not required to look for work as part of your benefit obligations. You'll continue to get your full benefit payment.

chunks.title: What you need to do
chunks.text: Community Work Experience means you need to find a position with a community or voluntary organisation for at least 5 hours a week, for 4 weeks. - You have 2 weeks to find a suitable position at a community or voluntary organisation, and complete and return the 'Community Work Experience' form. - Then you can start the 4 weeks Community Work Experience. - Once you finish, you need to get the organisation to sign the form and bring it to your appointment. You'll continue to get your full benefit payment until you've finished your Community Work Experience. Once you've finished and returned the signed declaration to us, you'll move back to green. Talk to us straight away if at any point you think you're not going to complete these steps.

chunks.title: Step 1 - Find an organisation and complete/return the form
chunks.text: You have up to 2 weeks to: - find a suitable position at a community or voluntary organisation, and - complete and return the 'Community Work Experience' form. Then we'll contact you to confirm you can start the Community Work Experience.

chunks.title: First, find a suitable position at a community or voluntary organisation
chunks.text: It needs to be a suitable organisation, like a charity, club, or marae. It also needs to be a suitable position, i.e. it's not paid and you're able to complete the activities required of you. You'll need to contact organisations to see if you can do Community Work Experience there. Make sure you can be there for at least 5 hours a week, for 4 weeks. You can find a position at more than one community or voluntary organisation if you want to.

chunks.title: Second, complete and return the form
chunks.text: We would have given you a 'Community Work Experience' form when you met with us while you were at orange in the traffic light system. Once you've found a community or voluntary organisation: - you need to complete pages 1 and 2 of the form, and - the organisation needs to complete pages 3 and 4 of the form. You need to keep pages 5 and 6 of the form. You need to drop pages 1-4 of this form into one of our offices before the 2 weeks is up. We need to confirm the position is suitable and approve the form before you start at the organisation. Find a service centre

chunks.title: Then we'll confirm you can start
chunks.text: If the position is suitable, we'll contact you straight away to let you know you can start. We'll also book an appointment for you to come in and see us the day after you're due to finish your Community Work Experience.

chunks.title: Step 2 - Be at the organisation for 4 weeks
chunks.text: You need to be at the organisation for at least 5 hours a week, for 4 weeks. You don't have to be there on weekends or public holidays, but you can if you want to. The organisation needs to be happy that you've completed the Community Work Experience satisfactorily.

chunks.title: Step 3 - Come to your appointment and bring the signed declaration
chunks.text: On the last day of your Community Work Experience, you need to give the organisation pages 5-6 of the form. They will complete it, sign the declaration and give it back to you. By signing it, they agree you’ve completed the Community Work Experience satisfactorily. You need to bring pages 5-6 with you to the appointment we booked for you the day after you finish. Once we've got the declaration, we'll move you back to green.

chunks.title: What happens if you don't complete these steps
chunks.text: Contact us straight away if you think you're not going to complete any of these steps. We'll talk to you about why this is the case. Phone us

chunks.title: If you have a good reason for not completing the steps
chunks.text: If you have a good reason, or if the position isn't suitable, we'll reduce your benefit by 50% and arrange for you to do a different activity. Once you've done the activity, you'll move back to green and get your full payment again.

chunks.title: If you don't have a good reason for not completing the steps
chunks.text: If you don't have a good reason, your benefit will either: - be paid at 50%, if you have dependent children, or - stop, if you don't have dependent children. We'll arrange for you to do a different activity. Once you've done the activity, you'll move back to green and get your full payment again. We'll stop or reduce your benefit from when you stopped participating with Community Work Experience. This means you may have a debt.

chunks.title: Compassionate grants
chunks.text: Compassionate grant lump sum payments don't need to be declared as income. But if you get Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit you do need to tell us about it.

chunks.title: What is this?
chunks.text: A compassionate grant can be paid by the government or another organisation, for example if your partner dies.

chunks.title: How it affects your benefit
chunks.text: If you: - get Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit you do need to tell us about your compassionate grant - invest the money you get and earn interest, this will be counted as income and you have to tell us about it.

chunks.title: Concerns or complaints about emergency housing
chunks.text: What happens if you have concerns or want to make a complaint about your emergency housing supplier. You have the same rights as any person under the law, like rights as a customer, and the right not to be discriminated against. If you have issues or concerns when staying in emergency housing: - Talk to your emergency housing supplier first. - Talk to us if there's no resolution. - Make a formal complaint if you feel like things haven't changed. You can withdraw your complaint at any time.

chunks.title: Issues or concerns when in emergency housing
chunks.text: Talk to your emergency housing supplier if you: - feel you're being treated unfairly, or - have concerns about the accommodation or services. You may be able to fix this together. If you feel the issue hasn't been sorted out in a reasonable time, talk to your case manager or youth coach. We may be able to help you discuss your concerns with the supplier. If nothing changes or the conditions become worse, you can make a formal complaint.

chunks.title: Making a formal complaint
chunks.text: If you choose to make a formal complaint about your emergency housing supplier, we’ll investigate this for you. You can either: - submit your complaint onlineexternal - call us on 0800 559 009 (you can book an appointment to come in and see us), or - write to us at Ministry of Social Development, PO Box 1556, Wellington. Submit your complaint online

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: We'll contact you to let you know we've received your complaint and what we'll do to resolve it. We'll also contact the emergency housing supplier to discuss the complaint with them. If your complaint is unique and complex and we need to work with others to resolve it, it may take longer. We’ll keep in touch with you while we do this. Once the complaint is resolved we'll send you and the supplier a letter about the outcome.

chunks.title: Withdrawing a complaint
chunks.text: You can withdraw your complaint at any time. You don’t have to wait until we’ve finished investigating your complaint. If you reach an agreement with the emergency housing supplier, you can call us on 0800 559 009 to let us know. We’ll send you and the supplier a letter confirming the complaint has been withdrawn.

chunks.title: Confirming IRD numbers
chunks.text: We may need to confirm your IRD number. Find out who this applies to, what we need, and how to get this to us. If you don’t know your IRD number, you can get this from the Inland Revenue website: Find my IRD number (Inland Revenue)external If we don't contact you, we've likely already confirmed your IRD number and you don't need to do anything. We're contacting everyone who's IRD number we need to confirm. Even if you think you already gave us your IRD number, we may need it again, or we may need your partner's. This may be because: - there's no IRD number on your file, or - the IRD number on your file doesn't match Inland Revenue’s information. Most of our clients already have a confirmed IRD number, and don't need to do anything.

chunks.title: Asking for your IRD number
chunks.text: If we need your IRD number, we'll call you first so you can tell us the number over the phone. If we can't sort it over the phone, we'll send you a letter, text or email asking for proof of your IRD number. Here's what you need to do to get it to us:

chunks.title: Step 1: Get proof
chunks.text: Proof of your IRD number can be either a: - letter from Inland Revenue (digital or paper) confirming your IRD number, or - screenshot of your myIR account (this needs to show your name, IRD number, Inland Revenue’s logo and the web address) – go here to log in Log in to myIR myIRexternal

chunks.title: Step 2: Get it to us
chunks.text: You can give proof of your IRD number to us by: - calling us so we can let you upload it to MyMSD, or - bringing it to a service centre so we can scan it. Phone us Find a service centre

chunks.title: Why this matters
chunks.text: If we've asked you for proof of your IRD number, you need to provide it by the date given in the letter – usually within 10 working days. If we don't get it in time, your payments may stop until we get it. If your payments stop, send us the proof as soon as possible. Once we have it, your payments will restart from the day they stopped. Everyone's situation is different – if you have a good reason for needing more time, or need help getting proof of your/your partner's IRD number, please call us before the due date. Phone us

chunks.title: How we use your IRD number
chunks.text: Benefits and pensions from us are taxed before they're paid to you. We need your IRD number to make sure your tax is going to the right Inland Revenue record. It also help us make sure we're paying the right person the right amount. For example, Inland Revenue may tell us if someone has earned income they haven’t told us about. This helps us act early and avoid overpayments. You can read more about this on Inland Revenue’s website, under ‘Disclosure of information for IRD validation’: Information sharing with Ministry of Social Development (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: Change of contact details
chunks.text: You need to tell us right away if your contact details change, eg phone number or email address. You can do this online, using MyMSD. You can update us on changes to your: - mobile phone number - home and work phone number - email address. You can also select which number you'd prefer us to contact you on. Most contact details can be updated right away.

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: If you can't use MyMSD you can call us. Phone us

chunks.title: Getting Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment
chunks.text: If you get Youth Payment or Young Parent Payment, you also need to contact your Youth Service provider directly to tell them about your change in circumstances. Contact (Youth Service)external

chunks.title: When we'll contact you
chunks.text: We may contact you for a number of reasons, eg: - when we need more information - when something's changed and we need to let you know - to talk to you about work or training opportunities. If we call you, our number will show as 0800 559 009. If you don't answer, we'll try again a bit later. You need to pick up when you can, or call us back. If we can't get hold of you, it may affect your payments.

chunks.title: Reviewing Childcare Subsidy payments
chunks.text: If you're getting childcare payments for your child and they haven't started school yet, your payments are reviewed every 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Why payments are reviewed
chunks.text: We'll check if: - you still need childcare - your circumstances have changed - the correct childcare rate is being paid. Your childcare payments may stop if you don't confirm this with us.

chunks.title: What you need to do
chunks.text: We'll send you a review form a few weeks before the review is due. - Complete the review form - even if you've updated your details for childcare recently. - You'll also be sent a verification form - get the supervisor at your child's childcare provider to sign. - You may need to provide proof of any income you have - the form will tell you what to provide. - Post the completed form to us (you'll find the address on the form) or you can email paperwork to us at Centralised_childcare_reviews@msd.govt.nz Find your nearest service centre

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: We'll let you know if your payments will continue for the next year. Or we may need to talk to you about your circumstances and changing your payments.

chunks.title: Confirm OSCAR Subsidy payments every term
chunks.text: If you want to keep getting childcare payments for before, after school and holiday care for your child, you need to confirm that with us every term.

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: We'll send you an Out of School Care and Recreation (OSCAR) declaration form to complete about a month before the school term ends. Or you can download the form. The form asks you to confirm your childcare arrangements, or let us know about any changes, eg, your child goes to after school care but now needs care in the holidays. - Download the OSCAR declaration form - Print the form and get your childcare provider to complete and sign the 'OSCAR Programme Supervisor to complete' section. - Post the completed form to your local service centre or you can email paperwork to us at Centralised_childcare_reviews@msd.govt.nz. If you can't print the form, contact us and we'll send one to you. Find your nearest service centre

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: If your child is in more than one programme, you need to complete a declaration form for each.

chunks.title: When you need to reapply
chunks.text: If it's been more than 8 weeks since you got the OSCAR Subsidy for before, after school or holiday care you'll need to apply again. OSCAR Subsidy You will also need to reapply if: - you want to enrol an additional child - your before, after school or holiday care payments have been cancelled.

chunks.title: Contraception
chunks.text: If you need contraception, there are a number of options available to you. Your decision whether to use contraceptives or not, and the type to use, is an entirely personal one made in consultation with a health practitioner, e.g. a doctor. You can talk to a health practitioner, e.g. your doctor, about what options are available. You can also get contraception at a lower cost or for free through some funded services. chunks.title: Cost of emergency housing
chunks.text: In most cases we'll cover the cost of your accommodation for the first 7 nights if you qualify. Then you'll have to start paying for some of the accommodation costs. This is called an Emergency Housing Contribution. In most cases we'll cover the cost of your accommodation for the first 7 nights if either: - it's your first time in emergency housing, or - it's been a while since you've needed emergency housing and there's a new reason you need it again.From the 8th night, you'll pay an Emergency Housing Contribution. If the emergency housing supplier also needs a security deposit, we can help with this. Security deposit for emergency housing

chunks.title: Emergency Housing Contribution
chunks.text: Below are the details of the Emergency Housing Contribution.

chunks.title: How much you have to pay
chunks.text: After 7 nights, you'll start to pay an Emergency Housing Contribution. You will need to pay the higher amount of either: - 25% of your and your partner's (if you have one) weekly income (after tax), or - 25% of the Jobseeker Support benefit rate you and your partner (if you have one) would qualify for (if you're not already getting it). Income may include payments from us, wages, salary or other income, or family tax credits. We'll let you know exactly how much your Emergency Housing Contribution will be and when you need to pay it by.

chunks.title: How to pay for it
chunks.text: If you get a main benefit, NZ Super or Veteran's Pension, it will automatically come out of your payment. Main benefit If you don't get a main benefit, NZ Super or Veteran's Pension, you can either: - set up an automatic payment (in the reference field put the letter 'E' followed by your 9 digit client number) - make a one-off payment to pay your contribution in full. There are different ways to do this, e.g. online or internet banking. See our Pay debt in NZ page for options of how to pay your contribution in full, or - pay the contribution directly from your wages - call our Client Support Debt Management team on 0800 558 0008 or email Client_Support_Debt_Management@msd.govt.nz How to repay debt from New Zealand

chunks.title: What happens if you don't pay it
chunks.text: You must pay your Emergency Housing Contribution on time. This is one of your responsibilities while in emergency housing. If you haven't paid it on time and you don't have a good reason, then either: - you'll get a warning, or - if you've had 2 warnings, your emergency housing grant will be declined and you won't be able to get it for 13 weeks. Your responsibilities while in emergency housing

chunks.title: Counselling
chunks.text: If you need help with counselling fees or transport to counselling, we may be able to pay this as part of a Disability Allowance. - You can get a Disability Allowance for a number of different things, including counselling. The maximum you can get for a Disability Allowance is $82.85 a week. - You don't have to be on a benefit to qualify for a Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You can apply for a Disability Allowance for you, your partner or a child. The person who needs counselling must: - have a health condition or disability that's likely to last at least 6 months from when they were diagnosed - need counselling because of the health condition or disability - have regular, ongoing counselling costs that are not fully covered by another agency (e.g. Oranga Tamariki, ACC). They also need to be seeing either: - a counsellor who is a member of: Psychotherapists Board of Aotearoa New Zealand NZ Association of Counsellors (NZAC) NZ Christian Counsellors Association The Social Workers Registration Board (SWRB) Australian, New Zealand and Asian Creative Arts Therapy Association (ANZACATA) - previously known as the Australian and New Zealand Arts Therapy Association (ANZATA) Drug and Alcohol Practitioners Association of Aotearoa New Zealand (DAPAANZ). This only includes Registered Competent Practitioners and Associate Practitioners. It does not include a support worker

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: - Psychotherapists Board of Aotearoa New Zealand - NZ Association of Counsellors (NZAC) - NZ Christian Counsellors Association - The Social Workers Registration Board (SWRB) - Australian, New Zealand and Asian Creative Arts Therapy Association (ANZACATA) - previously known as the Australian and New Zealand Arts Therapy Association (ANZATA) - Drug and Alcohol Practitioners Association of Aotearoa New Zealand (DAPAANZ). This only includes Registered Competent Practitioners and Associate Practitioners. It does not include a support worker - a psychologist who: holds a current practising certificate is registered with the Psychologists Board. - holds a current practising certificate - is registered with the Psychologists Board.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: To apply, you need to be: - 16 and older - a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident. It also depends on how much you and your partner earn.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: We pay up to a maximum of $82.85 a week for Disability Allowance. How much you get for counselling depends on your situation. If this is the first time you're applying for counselling, you can get up to 10 sessions. You can apply for more if a health practitioner, for example your doctor, recommends them.

chunks.title: We don't pay for:
chunks.text: - counselling not directly related to your disability or health condition, e.g. relationship counselling - counselling provided through hospitals (for example drug and alcohol), where no charge is made for these services (although we can pay for transport to these sessions) - the costs of childcare while you go to counselling.

chunks.title: Already getting payments from us (e.g. a benefit or Accommodation Supplement) but not Disability Allowance
chunks.text: - Complete a Disability Application for existing clients form. Your health practitioner (e.g. your doctor) will need to complete the Disability Certificate inside this form. - You need to complete a Disability Certificate - Counselling form. This needs to be completed by you, your health practitioner and your counsellor. Drop these documents off at one of our service centres, or post them to us: Find a service centre

chunks.title: Already getting Disability Allowance
chunks.text: You need to complete a Disability Certificate - Counselling form. This needs to be completed by you, your health practitioner and your counsellor. Drop these documents off at one of our service centres, or post them to us: Find a service centre We'll include the cost of counselling in your Disability Allowance from the date the cost started.

chunks.title: Not getting any payments from us
chunks.text: You can apply online. Apply online You'll also need to complete a Disability Certificate - Counselling form. This needs to be completed by you, your health practitioner and your counsellor. Drop these documents off at one of our service centres, or post them to us: Find a service centre

chunks.title: More than 10 sessions
chunks.text: We'll send you a letter when your 10 sessions are finished. If your health practitioner recommends you need more sessions: - You need to complete another Disability Certificate - Counselling form. This needs to be completed by you, your health practitioner and your counsellor. - you'll need to get your record of attendance (a form that your counsellor will get you to sign). Drop these documents off at one of our service centres, or post them to us: Find a service centre

chunks.title: Applying on behalf of someone else
chunks.text: You can apply for Disability Allowance on someone else's behalf, but only if they've filled out a form to appoint you as their agent. Having someone act on your behalf

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: It's your responsibility to agree with your counsellor on: - what you hope to get from the counselling - how many counselling sessions you'll need - how much you'll pay and how you'll pay for them. You'll have to pay for your counselling sessions directly to your counsellor or the organisation you're getting counselling through. To show us you've been going to the sessions, we may ask you for receipts and your record of attendance (your counsellor will complete that for you). Your counsellor will also get you to sign a form that lets them tell Work and Income about your attendance, and if you don't turn up for appointments or your counselling has ended.

chunks.title: Course Participation Assistance
chunks.text: We may be able to help with the costs of going to a short-term course or programme that helps you gain specific employment skills.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: To get Course Participation Assistance, you need to: - be on a benefit or stand-down for a benefit - be attending a short-term employment related course or programme that's 12 weeks or less - have specific costs because of your participation in a course or programme. It may also depend on: - how much you and your partner earn - any money or assets you and your partner have. Courses must be 12 weeks or less. They need to be either: - supplied by a provider who has a contract with Work and Income - approved by Work and Income - matched to a specific vacancy - specifically recognised alongside a Skills for Industry initiative, or - an Intensive Literacy and Numeracy programme or Targeted ESOL programme contracted by the Tertiary Education Commission.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: We can pay up to a maximum of $1,000 for: - course tuition and enrolment fees - transport to/from your course or programme - specific clothing required for your course or programme, and - care costs. How much you get depends on your circumstances.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: Once you’re clear about your career goal and what course you can take to help you get there, make an appointment with one of our case managers. Call us on 0800 559 009 We'll talk with you to understand your situation and how we can help. We'll let you know what information you need to provide and how to get this to us. You also need to fill out this form. We'll discuss the best way to get the completed form to us.

chunks.title: Payments to victims of crime
chunks.text: Lump-sum payments for victims of crimes don't need to be declared as income. But if you get Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit you do need to tell us about it.

chunks.title: What is it?
chunks.text: This is paid by Victim Support if you or your family are a victim of crime. This could be money to attend court, travel to court, or help with on-going or one-off expenses.

chunks.title: How it affects your benefit and allowances
chunks.text: You have to tell us about this payment if you: - get Accommodation Supplement, Temporary Additional Support or Special Benefit - invest the money you get and earn interest, after 12 months this will be counted as income.

chunks.title: Imprisoned or held in custody on remand
chunks.text: If you're imprisoned or held in custody on remand you need to tell us.

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: You, or someone you've appointed to act on your behalf, need to call us as soon as you can. If you don't, we may pay you too much and you'll have to pay this back. Phone us

chunks.title: Payments while you're in custody or remand
chunks.text: Your payments from us will stop the day after you enter custody – either sentenced or on remand. We'll send a letter to your home address and the prison you are being held at to confirm exactly what will happen to your payments and the date the payment will stop.

chunks.title: Still need payments while you're in custody
chunks.text: Your payments may be able to continue while you're in custody. This depends on your costs and circumstances, for example if you have: - a partner or dependent children - costs you must keep paying, like rent or hire purchase bills for essential items. If you still need your payments while you're in custody, contact us to talk about this. Your letter from us will tell you how to contact us.

chunks.text: While you're in prison or custody, you can appoint an agent to act on your behalf. How to choose someone to act on your behalf

chunks.title: CVs and cover letters
chunks.text: Take the hard work out of writing your CV and cover letter. Get advice about what to write, support to show you what to do, and free templates you can use. When you apply for a job, employers will look at your: - CV, to see your skills, any qualifications, and your work history - cover letter, to find out what kind of person you are and why you want this job. They'll use this to decide if they want to interview you, so it's really important to make a good impression.

chunks.title: 'Build my CV' service
chunks.text: A free service to help you write your CV and cover letter. It's run by the Auckland Business Chamber, and it's available online throughout New Zealand. You can get this if you're getting Jobseeker Support or Sole Parent Support. To sign up for ‘Build my CV’, call our Job Search line on 0800 779 009 or talk to your local service centre.

chunks.title: Te Heke Mai CV builder
chunks.text: An app to help when you're looking for work, including help to create a professional, polished CV. Te Heke Mai uses a fast and simple 7 step CV builder. You can also get personalised support and feedback. It's open to anyone in New Zealand. Find out more about Te Heke Maiexternal

chunks.title: How to write a cover letter
chunks.text: Careers.govt.nz has great advice about: - what your cover letter needs - how to make it look good - templates you can use. How to write a cover letter (tahatu.govt.nz)external

chunks.title: Your debt with us
chunks.text: We can help you manage any money you owe to Work and Income. When a debt is created, we'll check to see if this happened because of an error we made. If it's because of an error we made, we'll check against a list of criteria to see if we can write it off. If it wasn't because of an error we made, or we can't write it off, we'll send you a letter to let you know about it.

chunks.title: How we can help with your debt
chunks.text: If you have a debt with us, we're here to help. We can help with: - a breakdown of your debt, if you want one - debt repayments - what to do if you don't agree with your debt, and - support for managing your debt.

chunks.title: When you could get a debt
chunks.text: There are 2 common ways to get into debt with us: - We paid you too much money (an overpayment). This could happen if you didn't tell us: your correct income before we paid you about a change in your circumstances - your correct income before we paid you - about a change in your circumstances - We paid you money for something which you agreed to pay back. This is usually for something you really needed and couldn't afford at the time, e.g. a: washing machine, school uniform, or rent payment. - washing machine, - school uniform, or - rent payment.

chunks.title: Get a breakdown of your debt
chunks.text: If you want to get a breakdown of your debt, you can. How you get the breakdown depends on whether you get a benefit from us or not. - If you get a benefit from us, you'll be able to see a breakdown of your debt in MyMSD from 2018 onwards. If you want details of your debt from before 2018, you'll need to contact us. MyMSD login - If you don't get a benefit from us, you can contact us for a debt breakdown. If the debt breakdown is quite complex, it might take a few days to get this for you. It may be best for us to give it to you in writing as well. If this is the case, we'll let you know when you contact us.

chunks.title: How to contact us
chunks.text: If you're getting payments from us, call us on 0800 559 009 If you're not getting payments from us, contact our Client Support Debt Management Team. Client Support Debt Management Team Our staff will talk you through the debt and how it was created, and give you a breakdown of it.

chunks.title: Debt repayments
chunks.text: How much you repay and how you pay your debt back depends on whether you get one of these payments from us: - a main benefit - NZ Super or Veteran's pension, or - Accommodation Supplement. Repaying debt while getting one of these payments Repaying debt if you're not getting one of these payments

chunks.title: Disagree with your debt
chunks.text: If you think we've made a mistake with your debt, you can contact our Client Support - Debt Management Team. Client Support - Debt Management Team They can: - explain why you have a debt - consider any new information you give us - start a review of the decision if you ask them to. Review of a decision

chunks.title: Support for managing your debt
chunks.text: We have support to help you budget, deal with debt and manage your money. This includes information about: - budgeting support - MoneyTalks - a free financial helpline - joining a MoneyMates support group, and - talking to a financial mentor. Managing your money

chunks.title: Want someone else to talk with us about your debt
chunks.text: If you want someone else to talk with us about your debt, you need to fill out a form to nominate them as your agent. Having someone act on your behalf

chunks.title: If someone has died and had a debt with us
chunks.text: The debt becomes part of the person's estate, which is what a person owns and owes at the time they die. The debt won't be transferred or inherited by children, siblings, parents or any other relatives or friends. In most cases, the debt is not transferred to a surviving partner. The person's partner would only be liable if some of the debt was a shared debt from benefit fraud. We'll send a letter with information about the money owed to us. This letter is sent to the address of the person who died, or to whoever is settling their estate (if we know who it is). The letter will explain what to do. If there is money to pay it back from the person's estate, the letter will tell you how to pay this. If the estate doesn't have enough money to pay it, we may be able to write it off.

chunks.title: If someone has died and had a debt with us
chunks.text: If you want to get in touch about debt after death, please contact our Client Support Debt Management team: - phone 0800 558 008, or - email Client_Support_Debt_Management@msd.govt.nz

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Denmark
chunks.text: New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Denmark to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Danish payments (paid by Udbetaling Danmark). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers. Danish payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Security Pension - Anticipatory Pension - Disability Benefit - Labour Market Supplementary Pension. It also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.
