If they go to an overseas bank account, we'll pay the initial cost of transferring the funds. You must pay for any other costs that your bank charges. If they go to a NZ bank account, you must pay the cost of any transfers overseas.

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: Your NZ payments don’t have any tax taken off them. For information about your tax obligations, contact the tax authorities in the relevant countries. Irish Tax and Customs (Revenue)external Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: When your payments start from
chunks.text: We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation or Veterans Pension
chunks.text: Payment will usually start from the date of your application or the entitlement date. It will be whichever is later.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment, Sole Parent Support or Orphan's Benefit
chunks.text: There may be a stand-down period before we can pay you.

chunks.title: Send life certificates and renewal forms back to us
chunks.text: What type of form we'll send you and how often we send it depends on what NZ payment you get.

chunks.title: You get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you get NZ Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, we'll send you life certificates every 12 months. In some cases, we'll send you a life certificate every 6 months, e.g. if: - you use an agent, - your New Zealand Super or Veteran's Pension payments are made to a New Zealand bank account, or - you're over 80. You need to return the life certificate within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: You get Supported Living Payment, Sole Parent Support or Orphan's Benefit
chunks.text: If you get Supported Living Payment, Sole Parent Support or Orphan's Benefit, we'll send you a renewal form every 12 months. You need to return the renewal form within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: Travelling from Ireland to another country (not NZ)
chunks.text: Before you leave Ireland you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - Department of Social Protection, if you get an Irish payment. International Services team Department of Social Protection Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to the Department of Social Protection for information about what will happen to your Irish payment.

chunks.title: Temporarily visiting another country
chunks.text: If you're going to visit another country for 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. If you're going to visit another country for more than 26 weeks, your payments will stop from the date you leave Ireland. You may have a debt which you'll need to repay.

chunks.title: Moving to another country
chunks.text: NZ has Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with 11 countries. If you move to one of these countries, you'll need to re-apply for your NZ payment under the relevant agreement. One of the countries NZ has a SSA with is the United Kingdom (UK). If you're moving to the UK, you can't get an NZ payment. You may be able to get a UK payment instead under the UK Social Security Agreement. Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom (UK) - living in UK Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries If you move to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ, your New Zealand payment will stop.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand for 26 weeks or less, you'll get the same rate of payment you were getting in Ireland.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ permanently
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand permanently, you may be paid the full NZ rate less any payment you get from Ireland or another country. You need to contact us when you return to NZ so we can assess your payments. Phone us

chunks.title: Tell us about changes
chunks.text: You still need to tell us about any changes to your circumstances while you're living in Ireland. These changes may affect your payments. You also need to tell the Department of Social Protection about these changes. These changes could include: - entering a relationship, or - moving address. Contact International Services Contact the Department of Social Protection

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Jersey - living in Jersey
chunks.text: If you've lived in New Zealand and now live in Jersey, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Jersey to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Jersey payments (paid by the Jersey Social Security Department). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability. - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers. Jersey payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Pension - Sickness Benefit - Survivors Pension (formerly Widows Benefit) - Income Support Disablement - Incapacity Pension. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and Jersey payments
chunks.text: If you're already getting an NZ payment and going to live in Jersey, go to one of these pages to find out what you need to do: Living overseas if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension Living overseas while on a benefit If you're not already getting a NZ or Jersey payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in Jersey if you: - meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. However you will be ordinarily resident in Jersey instead of NZ when you apply - have been resident in NZ for at least 1 year from age 20 - are in New Zealand or Jersey when you apply, and - intend to be ordinarily resident in Jersey for at least 26 weeks from when you apply. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use your or your partner's time you've spent contributing to the Jersey insurance scheme to meet this criteria.

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get Supported Living Payment for a health condition, injury or disability while you're living in Jersey if you: - meet the criteria for Supported Living Payment - are 21 or older - have lived in New Zealand for at least 1 year from age 20 - are ordinarily resident in New Zealand when you apply, and - intend to live in Jersey for at least 26 weeks from when you apply. Supported Living Payment You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your or your partner's time you've spent contributing to the Jersey insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20.

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: Any overlapping periods can only be counted once.

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
chunks.text: You may be able to get Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower while you're living in Jersey if you: - meet the criteria for Sole Parent Support - are 21 or older - are the parent of one or more dependent children whose other parent is deceased - have lived in New Zealand for at least 1 year from age 20 - are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, and - intend to be live in Jersey for at least 26 weeks from when you apply. Sole Parent Support You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get Sole Parent Support. If you haven't, you may be able to use your or your late partner's time contributing to the Jersey insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20.

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
chunks.text: Any overlapping periods can only be counted once.

chunks.title: Who can get Jersey payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Jersey payments while you're living in Jersey. These are the: - Old Age Pension - Sickness Benefit - Survivors Pension (formerly Widows Benefit) - Income Support Disablement - Incapacity Pension. You may need to have lived in Jersey for a certain amount of time to get a Jersey payment. If so, you may be able to use periods of residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. However you will be ordinarily resident in the Netherlands instead of NZ when you apply - have been resident in NZ for at least 1 year continuously from age 20 - intend to live in the Netherlands for at least 26 weeks from when you apply, and - are in New Zealand or the Netherlands when you apply - are applying as a: widow and your child was conceived before your partner died, or widower and your child was born before your partner died. - widow and your child was conceived before your partner died, or - widower and your child was born before your partner died.

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows or widowers
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get Sole Parent Support. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you spent contributing to the national insurance scheme in the Netherlands from age 20 to meet this criteria. If you're applying for this benefit as a widow, you may also be able to use your late partner's contributions to the national insurance scheme. To use your or your late partner's time contributing to the national insurance scheme, you must have lived in NZ continuously for at least 1 year from age 20. Any overlapping periods can only be counted once. Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Who can get Netherlands payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Netherlands payments while you're living in the Netherlands. These are the: - Old Age Benefit - Survivors Benefit - Invalidity Benefit - Sickness Benefit - Unemployment Insurance (in certain circumstances regarding secondments to New Zealand) - Children's Allowances. You may need to have lived in the Netherlands for a certain amount of time to get a Netherlands payment. If so, you may be able to use periods of residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. The Netherlands social security agencies (Sociale Verzekeringsbank and Uitvoering Werknemersverzekeringen) decide who can get these Netherlands payments. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ payments
chunks.text: How you apply depends on if you're applying from NZ or the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Applying from NZ
chunks.text: You need to contact International Services at least 4 weeks before you leave NZ. They will book an appointment for you to come in and see us. At the interview, you and your partner (if you have one) will complete an application form. This includes questions about your residence in NZ. We'll ask you to bring these documents to the appointment: - your passport - another form of ID, e.g: birth certificate driver's licence marriage certificate - birth certificate - driver's licence - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - your travel itinerary or tickets - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into - any documentation that shows your intent to live in the Netherlands, e.g. an accommodation agreement.

chunks.title: Applying from NZ
chunks.text: You may need to bring other documents, we'll let you know when you call us.

chunks.title: Applying from the Netherlands
chunks.text: You need to contact the relevant Netherlands social security agency (Sociale Verzekeringsbank or Uitvoering Werknemersverzekeringen). You and your partner (if you have one) will need to complete an application form and provide proof of the time you lived in NZ. This proof can include: - testimonials - work references, and - letters from neighbours and friends. You'll also need to provide the following documents: - proof of your identity, e.g: birth certificate passport driver's licence, or marriage certificate - birth certificate - passport - driver's licence, or - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into, e.g: bank statement deposit slip.

chunks.title: Applying from the Netherlands
chunks.text: - bank statement - deposit slip. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: How to apply for Netherlands payments
chunks.text: You need to apply for Netherlands payments when you're in the Netherlands. Contact the relevant Netherlands social security agency to apply for these payments. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: New Zealand payments
chunks.text: If your NZ payments are made to a Netherlands bank account, the amount you get will change each month. This is because it depends on the exchange rate used to convert your payment from NZ dollars to Euros.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: How much you get is based on the number of months you lived in NZ from age 20. If you're born: - before 31 March 1936, contact us to find out how much you could get. - after 31 March 1936, we work out how much you could get using the steps below. Step 1: Confirm the number of months you've lived in New Zealand from age 20. Step 2: Divide this number by 540. Step 3: Take that answer and: - if you're single, multiply it by $1,191.14 (the single fortnightly gross rate we use), or - if you have a partner, multiply it by either: $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or $984.28 if you only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation).

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: - $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or - $984.28 if you only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation). For example, you're single and you've lived in NZ for 240 months (20 years) from age 20. Divide 240 by 540 which is 0.44. Then multiply this by the single gross rate of $1,191.14. That gives a fortnightly payment of $524.10 gross. Phone us

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support
chunks.text: How much you get depends on how many months you've lived in NZ from age 20. If you lived in New Zealand for: - 300 months (25 years) or more from age 20, you will get the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate or Sole Parent Support rate for your situation. - less than 300 months (25 years) from age 20, you need to: confirm the number of years you lived in NZ from age 20 divide this number by 300, and multiply this answer by the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate< or Sole Parent Support rate< for your situation. - confirm the number of years you lived in NZ from age 20 - divide this number by 300, and - multiply this answer by the maximum net Supported Living Payment rate< or Sole Parent Support rate< for your situation.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support
chunks.text: Supported Living Payment rate (Manuals and Procedures)external Sole Parent Support rate (Manuals and Procedures)external

chunks.title: Netherlands payments
chunks.text: The Netherlands social security agencies (Sociale Verzekeringsbank and Uitvoering Werknemersverzekeringen) decide how much you will be paid. For more information, contact the relevant agency. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: How you'll be paid
chunks.text: You can choose to have your payment made: - to an overseas bank account every 4 weeks, or - to a NZ bank account every 2 weeks. If they go to an overseas bank account, we'll pay the initial cost of transferring the funds. You must pay for any other costs that your bank charges. If they go to a NZ bank account, you must pay the cost of any transfers overseas.

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: Your NZ payments don't have any tax taken off them. For information about your tax obligations, contact the tax authorities in the relevant countries. Belastingdienst - Netherlands Tax Administrationexternal Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved.

chunks.title: New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Payment will usually start from the date of your application or the entitlement date. It will be whichever is later.

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support
chunks.text: There may be a stand-down period before we can pay you.

chunks.title: Send life certificates and renewal forms back to us
chunks.text: What type of form we'll send you and how often we send it depends on what NZ payment you get.

chunks.title: You get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you get NZ Superannuation or Veteran's Pension, we'll send you life certificates every 12 months. In some cases, we'll send you a life certificate every 6 months, e.g. if: - you use an agent, - your New Zealand Super or Veteran's Pension payments are made to a New Zealand bank account, or - you're over 80. You need to return the life certificate within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: You get Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support
chunks.text: If you get Supported Living Payment or Sole Parent Support, we'll send you a renewal form every 12 months. You need to return the renewal form within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: Travelling from the Netherlands to another country (not NZ)
chunks.text: Before you leave the Netherlands you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - the relevant Netherlands social security agency, if you get a Netherlands payment. Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to the relevant Netherlands social security agency for information about what will happen to your Netherlands payment. International Services

chunks.title: Temporarily visiting another country
chunks.text: If you're going to visit another country for 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. If you're going to visit another country for more than 26 weeks, your payments will be affected from the date you leave the Netherlands. You may have a debt which you'll need to repay.

chunks.title: Moving to another country
chunks.text: NZ has Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with 11 countries. If you move to one of these countries, you'll need to re-apply for your NZ payment under the relevant agreement. One of the countries NZ has a SSA with is the United Kingdom (UK). If you're moving to the UK, you can't get an NZ payment. You may be able to get a UK payment instead under the UK Social Security Agreement. Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom (UK) - living in UK Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries If you move to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ, your New Zealand payment will stop.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand for 26 weeks or less, you'll get the same rate of payment you were getting in the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ permanently
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand permanently, you may be paid the full NZ rate less any payment you get from the Netherlands or another country. You need to contact us when you return to NZ so we can assess your payments. Phone us

chunks.title: Tell us about changes
chunks.text: You still need to tell us about any changes to your circumstances while you're living in the Netherlands. These changes may affect your payments. You also need to tell the relevant Netherlands social security agency about these changes. These changes could include: - entering a relationship, or - moving address. Contact International Services Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Australia - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in Australia and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Australia to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an Australian citizen, - have an Australian residence class visa, or - are an New Zealand citizen.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Australian payments (paid by Centrelink). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability. Australian payments covered by this agreement are: - Australian Age Pension - Disability Support Pension - Carer Payment. It also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: Periods of residence
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super, Veteran's Pension and Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you may be able to use your Australian residence to meet this criteria. Contact our International Services team if you want to talk about your situation. International Services

chunks.title: Periods of residence for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Find out if you can use your Australian residence for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension: Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Periods of residence for Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: To use your Australian residence for Supported Living Payment, you must have: - been living in Australia during that time, and - been an Australian resident for 12 months, of which at least 6 months were continuous.

chunks.title: NZ and Australian payments
chunks.text: If you already get an Australian payment and move to NZ, contact Centrelink. They'll change the payment if needed. Contact us (Services Australia)external If you're not already getting a NZ or Australian payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in New Zealand. To get this you must meet the eligibility criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension If you don't meet the eligibility criteria, you may still qualify if you meet the following criteria: - you are 67 or older (the age criteria for Australian Age Pension) - you have lived in Australia (as defined by Centrelink) for at least 12 months between age 20 and age 67 (the age you qualify for Australian Age Pension), of which 6 months were continuous - you either: are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: - are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or - intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply Ordinarily resident - you either: have lived in NZ for a certain number of years since you turned 20, with 5 years since the age of 50. How many years you need is based on your date of birth (you can work this out on our 'Who can get NZ Super' page). You can use time spent as an Australian resident between age 20 and age 67 (the age you qualify for Australian Age Pension) to count towards this, or are in New Zealand when you apply. - have lived in NZ for a certain number of years since you turned 20, with 5 years since the age of 50. How many years you need is based on your date of birth (you can work this out on our 'Who can get NZ Super' page). You can use time spent as an Australian resident between age 20 and age 67 (the age you qualify for Australian Age Pension) to count towards this, or

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: - are in New Zealand when you apply. For Veteran's Pension you also need to have the necessary service and disability qualifications. Who can get Australian Age Pension (Services Australia)external Definition of Australian resident and living in Australia (Services Australia)external

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get Supported Living Payment while you're living in New Zealand. To get this you must meet the eligibility criteria for Supported Living Payment. If you don't meet the eligibility criteria, you may still qualify if you meet the following criteria: - you either: are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply - are ordinarily resident in NZ when you apply, or - intend to remain in New Zealand for at least 1 year or have lived in NZ for at least 6 months before you apply, and are in New Zealand when you apply - you have a total of 2 years residence in New Zealand and/or Australia

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: - you have lived in Australia (as defined by Centrelink) for at least 12 months, of which 6 months were continuous, and - you are medically assessed as 'severely disabled' - this means: you must either: be permanently blind, or have a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment that means you cannot work or benefit from any assistance or rehabilitation programme for the next 2 years, and the severe disablement happened while you were living in New Zealand or Australia. - you must either: be permanently blind, or have a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment that means you cannot work or benefit from any assistance or rehabilitation programme for the next 2 years, and - be permanently blind, or

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: - have a physical, psychiatric or intellectual impairment that means you cannot work or benefit from any assistance or rehabilitation programme for the next 2 years, and - the severe disablement happened while you were living in New Zealand or Australia. Ordinarily resident Definition of Australian resident and living in Australia (Services Australia)external

chunks.title: Who can get Australian payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Australian payments while you're living in NZ. CentreLink in Australia decides who can get the Australian payments. How to contact Services Australiaexternal

chunks.title: How to apply for Australian payments
chunks.text: Contact International Services to find out what Australian payments you can get. International Services They will send you an application form to complete. You need to fill it out and send it back to them. They will then forward your application to Centrelink in Australia who will process it. Once a decision has been made, International Services will be in touch with you to let you know the outcome.

chunks.title: How to apply for New Zealand payments
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. Check what you might getexternal

chunks.title: How much you'll get
chunks.text: Your total payment will be made up of: - a NZ payment, and - an Australian payment - Centrelink calculates and pays the Australian payment.

chunks.title: NZ payment rates
chunks.text: For NZ payments, you'll get the NZ rates for the payment you qualify for. - NZ Super or Veteran's Pension rates - Supported Living Payment rates How much you can get for NZ Super Supported Living Payment (current)external If you or your partner qualify for an overseas pension, this could affect your NZ rate. The Australian payment from Centrelink is classed as an overseas pension. Overseas pensions

chunks.title: Australian payment rates
chunks.text: Talk to Centrelink for information about how they calculate the Australian rate.

chunks.title: How you'll be paid
chunks.text: If you're living in NZ, you can choose to have your Australian payment paid by either the: - Direct Payment Method, or - Special Banking option. Payment options for overseas pensions

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: You may have to pay tax on your Australian payment in New Zealand if you: - are paid your Australian pension by the Direct Payment Method. This is regardless of whether it's paid to a bank account in Australia or NZ, and - get NZ Super or Veteran’s Pension. Make sure you keep copies of all your banking records. These may show your gross Australian pension payments required for tax purposes.

chunks.title: If you get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you're paid your Australian pension by Direct Payment Method, you do not have to pay tax. This is because your gross Australian payment is deducted directly from your net New Zealand entitlement. However if your Australian payments are more than the maximum Supported Living Payment, you will need to pay tax.

chunks.title: Special Banking option
chunks.text: If you have chosen the Special Banking Option, the tax is already paid before you get your payment. However, you may need to pay tax on any Australian payment you got prior to choosing the Special Banking Option. You can talk to Inland Revenue New Zealand about your tax liability. Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: NZ payments will start from the date of your application or the entitlement date - whichever is later. We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved. Centrelink decides when you get paid any Australian payments.

chunks.title: Travelling from NZ to another country (not Australia)
chunks.text: Before you leave NZ you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - Centrelink, if you get an Australian payment. International Services Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to Centrelink for information about what will happen to your Australian payment.

chunks.title: NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you're going to another country for: - 26 weeks or less, your payment may continue while you're away. There are certain criteria you'll need to meet. - more than 26 weeks, you may be able to apply to keep your payments going. Travelling overseas for 26 weeks or less

chunks.title: Going for more than 26 weeks
chunks.text: You may have had to use your Australian residence to help you meet the residence criteria for your NZ payment. If you used your Australian residence and: - still need to do this to meet the residence criteria, your payments will stop from the day after you leave New Zealand. When you come back to NZ, you'll have to re-apply to get this payment again. - no longer need to do this to meet the residence criteria, you may be able to apply to get some or all of your NZ payment. What you're paid depends on what country you go to. You need to apply before you leave NZ. If you qualify to be paid in that country, payment will be made from the first payment date after you leave NZ. Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: If you're going to another country, your Supported Living Payment may continue. It depends if the country you're going to has a SSA with NZ and what that agreement states.

chunks.title: Going to a country that has a SSA with NZ
chunks.text: You may be able to apply to keep your payments going. It depends what the agreement states and if it covers you to be paid Supported Living Payment. You need to apply before you leave NZ, otherwise your payments will stop after you leave NZ.

chunks.title: Going to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ
chunks.text: If you move to that country, your payments will stop after you leave NZ. If you're going to that country temporarily, you may be able to keep getting your Supported Living Payment. It depends on why you're going there. Going overseas temporarily while on a benefit

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Malta - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in Malta and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Malta to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Maltese payments (paid by the Maltese Department of Social Security). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension. Maltese payments covered by this agreement are: - Retirement Pension - Survivor's Pension - Non-contributory Old Age Pension. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and Maltese payments
chunks.text: If you already get a Maltese payment and move to NZ, contact the Maltese Department of Social Security. They'll change the payment if needed. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security If you're not already getting a NZ or Maltese payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in Malta, and - you meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent contributing to the Maltese insurance scheme to meet this criteria. To include this time, you must: - have at least 1 year of continuous NZ working age residence, and - be ordinarily resident in NZ. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get Maltese payments
chunks.text: You may be able to get Maltese payments while you're living in NZ. These are the: - Retirement Pension - Survivor's Pension - Non-contributory Old Age Pension. You may need to have lived in Malta for a certain amount of time to get a Maltese payment. If so, you may be able to use periods of residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. The Maltese Department of Social Security decides who can get these Maltese payments. Department of Social Security Maltaexternal Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ payments
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. You also need to apply for: - any Maltese payment that you may qualify for and - any other overseas payments that you may be able to get. Check What You Might Getexternal

chunks.title: How to apply for Maltese payments
chunks.text: You should apply through the Maltese Department of Social Security before you leave Malta. If you already live in New Zealand, contact our International Services team. They'll send you an application form to complete and you'll need to send it back to them. Then they'll forward that to the Maltese Department of Social Security. International Services The Maltese Department of Social Security will decide whether you can get a Maltese payment and let you know. This may take a few months. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: New Zealand payments
chunks.text: We'll decide how much you will be paid based on certain criteria. If you get an overseas pension, it's usually deducted from your New Zealand payment. Overseas pensions Generally, the amount you're paid is about equal to what you would be paid if you had lived all your life in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Maltese payments
chunks.text: The Maltese Department of Social Security decides how much you will be paid. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: NZ payments
chunks.text: NZ Super and Veteran's Pension payments are paid into your nominated NZ bank account fortnightly.

chunks.title: Maltese payments
chunks.text: Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security to find out how Maltese payments are paid. Contact the Maltese Department of Social Security

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: - You have to pay NZ tax on your NZ payments. We'll withhold your NZ tax based on the tax code you're using and pay this directly to the NZ tax department, Inland Revenue. - You may have to pay NZ tax on your Maltese payment. This is regardless of whether it's paid to a bank account in Malta or NZ. - You may have to pay Maltese tax on your Maltese payment. For more information, talk to the Maltese tax authority. If your Maltese payment is liable for tax in Malta, you may be able to get a rebate on your New Zealand tax. We recommend you discuss your tax liabilities with the relevant tax agency. Inland Revenueexternal Tax & Customs Administration Maltaexternal

chunks.title: Keep copies of your bank records
chunks.text: Make sure you keep copies of all your banking records, as these may show your gross Maltese pension payments required for tax purposes.

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: NZ payments will start from the date of your application or the entitlement date - whichever is later. We'll let you know what date this will be in the letter we send you, once your application's approved. The Maltese Department of Social Security decides when you get paid any Maltese payments.

chunks.title: Travelling from NZ to another country (not Malta)
chunks.text: Before you leave New Zealand you need to contact: - our International Services team - the Maltese Department of Social Security, if you get a Maltese payment. International Services Department of Social Security Malta You may keep getting your NZ payment but it depends on: - where you're going - how long you're going for, and - what type of payment you're getting. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call. Talk to the Maltese Department of Social Security for information about what will happen to your Maltese payment.

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with South Korea - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in South Korea and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with South Korea to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or South Korean payments (paid by the South Korean National Pension Service). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension. The only South Korean payment covered by this agreement is the Old-age Pension. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and South Korean payments
chunks.text: If you already get the Old-age Pension and move to NZ, contact the South Korean National Pension Service. They'll change the payment if needed. South Korean National Pension Service If you're not already getting a NZ or South Korean payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in South Korea, and - you meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent contributing to the Korean National Pension Scheme from age 20 to meet this criteria. To use this time, you must: - have at least 1 year of continuous NZ working age residence, and - be ordinarily resident in NZ. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get Old-age Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get the Old-age Pension while you're living in NZ. You must have contributed to the Korean National Pension Scheme for a certain amount of time to get this payment. You may be able to use periods of working age residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. The South Korean National Pension Service decides who can get the Old-age Pension. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Use our Check What You Might Get tool to find out what NZ payments you can get and how to apply. Check What You Might Getexternal You also need to apply for: - any South Korean payment that you may qualify for and - any other overseas payments that you may be able to get.

chunks.title: How to apply for the Old-age Pension
chunks.text: You should apply through the South Korean National Pension Service before you leave South Korea. If you already live in New Zealand, contact our International Services team. They'll send you an application form to complete and you'll need to send it back to them. Then they'll forward that to the South Korean National Pension Service. The South Korean National Pension Service will decide whether you can get the Old-age Pension and let you know. This may take a few months. chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with Canada - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in Canada and now live in New Zealand, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with Canada to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or Canadian payments (paid by Service Canada). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability - Sole Parent Support for widows and widowers Canadian payments covered by this agreement are: - Old Age Security Pension - Canada Pension Plan (if you get the Quebec Pension Plan, this is not covered by the agreement). This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in NZ and Canadian creditable periods so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and Canadian payments
chunks.text: If you already get a Canadian payment and move to NZ, contact Service Canada. They'll change the payment if needed. If you're not already getting a NZ or Canadian payment, read the information below. Contact the Government of Canadaexternal

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom - living in New Zealand
chunks.text: If you've lived in the United Kingdom (UK) and now live in New Zealand (NZ), you may be able to get some payments. This is because NZ has an agreement with the UK to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or UK payments (paid by the International Pension Centre). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - NZ Superannuation - Supported Living Payment, where you have a health condition, injury or disability - Sole Parent Support for widows - Orphan's Benefit - Jobseeker Support. UK payments covered by this agreement are: - State Pension - Widow's Benefits and Bereavement Benefits - Incapacity Benefits - Guardians’ Allowance - Child Benefit. It also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and UK payments
chunks.text: If you already get a UK payment and move to NZ, contact the International Pension Centre. They'll change the payment if needed. International Pension Centreexternal If you're not already getting a NZ or UK payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in the UK, and - you meet the criteria for NZ Super. Who can get NZ Super You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super. If you haven't, you can meet this criteria by using the amount of time you've spent either: - living in the UK, or - living outside of the UK from age 20 and paying contributions to the UK National Insurance scheme. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super

chunks.title: Who can get Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: You may be able to get Supported Living Payment for a health condition, injury or disability while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in the UK, and - you meet the NZ criteria for Supported Living Payment You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years to get Supported Living Payment. If you haven't, you can use the amount of time you've spent living in the UK to meet this criteria. Supported Living Payment

chunks.title: Who can get Sole Parent Support for widows
chunks.text: You may be able to get Sole Parent Support as a widow or widower while you're living in NZ if: - you've lived in the UK, and - you meet the NZ criteria for Sole Parent Support You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 2 years to get Sole Parent Support for widows. Sole Parent Support

chunks.title: Who can get Jobseeker Support

Jobseeker Support

chunks.title: How to apply for UK payments

Overseas pensions Generally, the amount you're paid is about equal to what you would be paid if you had lived all your life in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Netherlands payments
chunks.text: The Netherlands Social Security Agencies decide how much you will be paid. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: NZ payments
chunks.text: NZ payments are paid into your nominated NZ bank account. NZ Super and Veteran's Pension are paid fortnightly. All other NZ payments are paid weekly.

chunks.title: Netherlands payments
chunks.text: Contact the relevant Netherlands social security agency to find out how Netherlands payments are paid. Contact the Netherlands social security agencies

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: - You have to pay NZ tax on your NZ payments. We'll withhold your NZ tax based on the tax code you're using and pay this directly to the NZ tax department, Inland Revenue. - You may have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands holiday pay and voluntary contributions. - You may have to pay Netherlands tax on your Netherlands payment. For more information, talk to the Netherlands Tax Administration - Belastingdienst. If your Netherlands payment is liable for tax in the Netherlands, you may be able to get a rebate on your New Zealand tax. Individuals living or working outside the Netherlands (Belastingdienst)external

chunks.title: Paying NZ tax on your Netherlands payment
chunks.text: You may have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payment, it depends what NZ payment you get. Generally you will have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payments. However you may not have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payment if it's paid by Special Banking Option (unless it's holiday pay or voluntary contributions that are passed onto you). If you took up the Special Banking Option part way through a tax year, you may still have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payment. This is regardless of whether it's paid to a bank account in the Netherlands or NZ. Generally you will have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payments. However you may not have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payment if it's paid by the Direct Payment Method (unless it's holiday pay or voluntary contributions).

chunks.title: Paying NZ tax on your Netherlands payment
chunks.text: If your Netherlands payment is more than your benefit, you won't get your main benefit and you'll only get the Netherlands payment. In this case you may have to pay NZ tax on your Netherlands payment.

chunks.title: Keep copies of your bank records
chunks.text: Make sure you keep copies of all your banking records, as these may show your gross Netherlands pension payments required for tax purposes.

chunks.title: Talk to the NZ tax agency
chunks.text: We recommend you discuss your tax liabilities with Inland Revenue (New Zealand). Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: NZ payments will start from the date of your application or the entitlement date - whichever is later. We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved. The Netherlands social security agencies decide when you get paid any Netherlands payments.

chunks.title: Travelling from NZ to another country (not the Netherlands)
chunks.text: Before you leave New Zealand you need to contact: - our International Services team - the relevant Netherlands social security agency, if you get a Netherlands payment. International Services team Contact the Netherlands social security agency You may keep getting your NZ payment but it depends on: - where you're going - how long you're going for, and - what type of payment you're getting. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call. Talk to the relevant Netherlands social security agency for information about what will happen to your Netherlands payment.

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with South Korea - living in South Korea
chunks.text: If you've lived in New Zealand and now live in South Korea, you may be able to get some payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with South Korea to share responsibility for social security coverage. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for certain NZ payments (paid by us) or South Korean payments (paid by the South Korean National Pension Service). NZ payments covered by this agreement are: - New Zealand Superannuation (NZ Super) - Veteran's Pension. The only South Korean payment covered by this agreement is the Old-age Pension. This agreement also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: NZ and South Korean payments
chunks.text: If you're already getting an NZ payment and going to live in South Korea, go to one of these pages to find out what you need to do: Living overseas if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension Living overseas while on a benefit If you're not already getting a NZ or South Korean payment, read the information below.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension while you're living in South Korea if you: - meet the criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. However you will be ordinarily resident in South Korea instead of NZ when you apply - have lived in New Zealand for at least 1 year continuously between ages 20 and 65 - are in New Zealand or South Korea when you apply, and - intend to live in South Korea for at least 26 weeks from when you apply. Who can get NZ Super Who can get Veteran's Pension You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've spent contributing to a Korean scheme from age 20 to meet this criteria.

chunks.title: Who can get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: To use this time, you must: - have at least 1 year of continuous NZ working age residence, and - be ordinarily resident and present in NZ or South Korea when you apply. Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

chunks.title: Who can get the Old-age Pension
chunks.text: You may be able to get the Old-age Pension while you're living in South Korea. You must have contributed to the Korean National Pension Scheme for a certain amount of time to get this payment. You may be able to use periods of working age residence in New Zealand to meet this criteria. The South Korean National Pension Service decides who can get the Old-age Pension. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: How to apply for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: How you apply depends on if you're applying from NZ or South Korea.

chunks.title: Applying from NZ
chunks.text: You need to contact International Services at least 4 weeks before you leave NZ. They will book an appointment for you to come in and see us. At the appointment, you and your partner (if you have one) will complete an application form. This includes questions about your residence in NZ. We'll ask you to bring these documents to the appointment: - your passport - another form of ID, e.g: birth certificate driver's licence marriage certificate - birth certificate - driver's licence - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - your travel itinerary or tickets - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into - any documentation that shows your intent to live in South Korea, e.g. an accommodation agreement.

chunks.title: Applying from NZ
chunks.text: You may need to bring other documents, we'll let you know when you call us.

chunks.title: Applying from South Korea
chunks.text: You need to contact the South Korean National Pension Service. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service You and your partner (if you have one) will need to complete an application form and provide proof of the time you lived in NZ. This proof can include: - testimonials - work references, and - letters from neighbours and friends. You'll also need to provide the following documents: - proof of your identity, e.g: birth certificate passport driver's licence, or marriage certificate - birth certificate - passport - driver's licence, or - marriage certificate - proof of NZ residency - bank account details for the account you want your payments to go into, e.g: bank statement deposit slip. - bank statement

chunks.title: Applying from South Korea
chunks.text: - deposit slip. The South Korean National Pension Service will send your application form to us. We'll check if you meet the criteria and send you a letter to let you know the outcome.

chunks.title: How to apply for the Old-age Pension
chunks.text: Contact the South Korean National Pension Service to apply. They will confirm whether you meet the criteria and your payment amount, and send you a letter to confirm. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If your NZ payments are made to a South Korean bank account, the amount you get will change each month. This is because it depends on the exchange rate used to convert your payment from NZ dollars to won. How much you get is based on the number of months you lived in NZ between the ages of 20 and 65. This is a total of 540 months (or 45 years). We work out how much you could get using the steps below. Step 1: Confirm the number of months you've lived in New Zealand from age 20 to 65. Step 2: Divide this number by 540. Step 3: Take that answer and: - if you're single, multiply it by $1,191.14 (the single fortnightly gross rate we use), or - if you have a partner, multiply it by either: $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or $984.28 if you only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation).

chunks.title: NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: - $1,968.56 if both you and your partner qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation), or - $984.28 if you only you qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension (the couple fortnightly gross rate for this situation). For example, you're single and you've lived in NZ for 240 months (20 years) from age 20. Divide 240 by 540 which is 0.44. Then multiply this by the single gross rate of $1,191.14. That gives a fortnightly payment of $524.10 gross.

chunks.title: Old-age Pension
chunks.text: The South Korean National Pension Service decides how much you will be paid. For more information, contact the South Korean National Pension Service. Contact the South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: How you'll be paid
chunks.text: You can choose to have your payment made: - to an overseas bank account every 4 weeks, or - to a NZ bank account every 2 weeks. If they go to an overseas bank account, we'll pay the initial cost of transferring the funds. You must pay for any other costs that your bank charges. If they go to a NZ bank account, you must pay the cost of any transfers overseas.

chunks.title: Taxes
chunks.text: Your NZ payments don't have any tax taken off them. For information about your tax obligations, contact the tax authorities in the relevant countries. South Korean National Tax Serviceexternal Inland Revenueexternal

chunks.title: When your payments will start from
chunks.text: Payment will usually start from the date of your application or the entitlement date. It will be whichever is later. We'll let you know what date your payment will start in the letter we send you, once your application's approved.

chunks.title: Send Client Declaration forms back to us
chunks.text: We'll send you Client Declaration forms every 12 months if you get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. In some cases, we'll send you a Client Declaration form every 6 months, e.g. if: - you use an agent, - your New Zealand Super or Veteran's Pension payments are made to a New Zealand bank account, or - you're over 80. You need to fill in the form and get it certified by either a: - magistrate - NZ embassy employee, or - Justice of the Peace (or the South Korean equivalent). Then you need to return this form within 8 weeks otherwise your payments will stop.

chunks.title: Travelling from South Korea to another country (not NZ)
chunks.text: Before you leave South Korea you need to contact: - our International Services team, and - the South Korean National Pension Service, if you get a South Korean payment. International Services South Korean National Pension Service Below are details of what will happen to your NZ payments. Our International Services team will talk you through this when you call and tell you what you need to do. Talk to the South Korean National Pension Service for information about what will happen to your South Korean payment.

chunks.title: Temporarily visiting another country
chunks.text: If you're going to visit another country for 26 weeks or less, your payments will continue while you're away. If you're going to visit another country for more than 26 weeks, your payments will stop from the date you leave South Korea. You may have a debt which you'll need to repay.

chunks.title: Moving to another country
chunks.text: NZ has Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with 11 countries. If you move to one of these countries, you'll need to re-apply for your NZ payment under the relevant agreement. One of the countries NZ has a SSA with is the United Kingdom (UK). If you're moving to the UK, you can't get an NZ payment. You may be able to get a UK payment instead under the UK Social Security Agreement. Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom (UK) - living in UK Social Security Agreements and special arrangements with Pacific countries If you move to a country that doesn't have a SSA with NZ, your New Zealand payment will stop.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ temporarily
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand for 26 weeks or less, you'll get the same rate of payment you were getting in South Korea.

chunks.title: Returning to NZ permanently
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand permanently, you may be paid the full NZ rate less any payment you get from South Korea or another country. You need to contact us when you return to NZ so we can assess your payments. Phone us

chunks.title: Tell us about changes
chunks.text: You still need to tell us about any changes to your circumstances while you're living in South Korea. These changes may affect your payments. You also need to tell the South Korean National Pension Service about these changes. These changes could include: - entering a relationship, or - moving address. Contact International Services Contact South Korean National Pension Service

chunks.title: Social Security Agreement with the United Kingdom (UK) - living in UK
chunks.text: If you've lived in New Zealand and now live in the United Kingdom (UK), you may be able to get some UK payments. This is because New Zealand (NZ) has an agreement with the UK to share responsibility for social security coverage. You can't get any NZ payments under this agreement. This agreement can help you if you either: - are an NZ citizen - are an NZ permanent resident, or - have an NZ resident visa.

chunks.title: How this Social Security Agreement helps you
chunks.text: This agreement generally allows you to apply for these UK payments (paid by the International Pension Centre): - State Pension - Widow's Benefits and Bereavement Benefits - Incapacity Benefits - Guardians’ Allowance - Child Benefit - Job Seekers Allowance. It also allows you to add together your periods of residence in either country so you can meet certain criteria for these payments.

chunks.title: Who can get these UK payments
chunks.text: If you live in the UK, you may be able to get UK payments if you have either: - lived in New Zealand for long enough, or - made enough contributions to the United Kingdom National Insurance Scheme. You may also be able to use periods of residence in New Zealand to meet the criteria for a UK payment. The International Pension Centre in the United Kingdom decides who can get UK benefits and pensions. International Pension Centreexternal

chunks.title: How to apply for UK payments
chunks.text: You must be in the United Kingdom to apply for United Kingdom payments. You need to apply through the UK International Pension Centre. International Pension Centreexternal

chunks.title: How much you'll get for UK payments
chunks.text: The UK International Pension Centre will decide how much you'll be paid.

chunks.title: How and when you'll be paid
chunks.text: The UK International Pension Centre will let you know how and when you'll get paid. You may need to open a UK bank account.

chunks.title: Living overseas while on a benefit
chunks.text: If you get a main benefit from us and are going to live overseas, you may be able to keep getting your benefit payment. It depends which country you're moving to and what benefit you get. You can't get any other payments from us while you're living overseas, such as Accommodation Supplement, Disability Allowance and Winter Energy Payment. You must tell us you're going overseas before you leave New Zealand. There are different rules if you: - are going overseas temporarilyexternal while on a main benefit, or - get New Zealand Superannuation or Veteran's Pensionexternal.

chunks.title: Countries where your benefit may continue
chunks.text: If you’re moving to a country that’s not an SSA country, your payment will stop. In most cases you can't get payments from us while you're living overseas. In these countries you may be able to keep getting a benefit payment: - Australia - Canada - Denmark - Greece - Ireland - Jersey - Guernsey, and - Netherlands. There are three countries where your New Zealand benefit cannot be paid, but you may be able to get a payment from that country’s Social Security Agency based on your time in New Zealand: - Malta - South Korea, and - United Kingdom (UK).

chunks.title: Moving to an SSA country
chunks.text: Select the country you're moving to, to find out what main benefit payments may continue.

chunks.title: Australia
chunks.text: You may be able to keep getting Supported Living Payment. All other main benefit payments from us will stop. For your Supported Living Payment to continue, you need to do certain things. What you need to do depends on whether you already get Australian Disability Support Pension or not.

chunks.title: You don't already get Australian Disability Support Pension
chunks.text: Your Supported Living Payment will continue after leaving NZ if you: - qualify for the Australian Disability Support Pension - apply for the Australian Disability Support Pension within 4 weeks of leaving NZ, and - apply to get your Supported Living Payment Overseas - you need to apply within 1 year of applying for Australian Disability Support Pension. Who can get Disability Support Pension - Services Australiaexternal After 4 weeks your Supported Living Payment will stop. If you don't apply for the Australian Disability Support Pension within those 4 weeks, you will need to pay back any money you received from the day you left NZ. If you apply for the Australian Disability Support Pension within those 4 weeks, you must also apply for the Supported Living Payment Overseas within 1 year. If you don't, you'll need to repay any payments you received from us from the day after you left NZ.

chunks.title: You already get Australian Disability Support Pension
chunks.text: You must apply to continue to receive your Supported Living Payment within 4 weeks of leaving New Zealand or you’ll need to pay back any payments received after leaving New Zealand. After 4 weeks your payment may stop, and you may experience a gap in payments. However, if you apply within the first four weeks your payment will be backdated.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You need to: - contact our International Services team before you leave NZ. Let them know the date you're leaving. - contact Services Australia within the first 4 weeks of leaving NZ to either: - claim an Australian Disability Support Pension from them - if you're not already receiving it, or - apply to continue to get your Supported Living Payment - if you're already receiving Australian Disability Support Pension. Contact our International Services teamexternal Contact Services Australiaexternal Once Services Australia have processed your Australian Disability Support Pension form, they will send you a NZ payment application form. This form is to apply for your Supported Living Payment Overseas. You need to complete this form and send it back to Services Australia.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: We'll get a copy of the form and use it to work out: - if you qualify for Supported Living Payment Overseas, and - how much you can be paid.

chunks.title: If Australian Disability Support Pension is declined
chunks.text: If your Australian Disability Support Pension application is declined because of: - your income or assets, we'll most likely decline your NZ payment application. - not meeting Centrelink’s definition of ‘severely disabled’, we’ll most likely decline your application. - another reason, e.g. residency requirements, we may still approve your NZ payment application. If we decline your NZ payment application, your Supported Living Payment will stop from the date your Australian Disability Support Pension is declined. We'll then review the NZ payments you received since you left NZ. We do this to make sure you were getting the right amount of payment during this time. Contact International Servicesexternal

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: You’ll get your Supported Living Payment at the same rate you would get if you lived in NZ for the first four weeks you are in Australia. Changes to this rate will start once: - your Australian Disability Support Pension is approved, and - your NZ payment application is approved. How much you get depends on how long you've lived in New Zealand since you were 20 years old. If you get SLP and have a partner, they can be included in your payments These rate changes will then be backdated to the date you applied for Australian Disability Support Pension. For example, if you applied for this within one week of leaving NZ, your rate change will be backdated to week one.

chunks.title: More information
chunks.text: More information about getting Supported Living Payment in Australia can be found on our Australian Social Security Agreement page. Social Security Agreement with Australia - living in Australiaexternal

chunks.title: Canada, Denmark, Greece, Ireland, Jersey, Guernsey or the Netherlands
chunks.text: You may be able to keep getting either the: - Supported Living Payment (SLP), if you're getting this because you have a health condition, injury or disability - Sole Parent Support (SPS) if you're getting this because you're a widow or widower, or - Orphan's Benefit, if you're going to Greece or Ireland. All other main benefit payments from us will stop. If you have been living in Greece there may be eligibility for a Funeral Grant How much you get for SLP or SPS depends on how long you've lived in New Zealand since you were 20 years old. If you get SLP and have a partner, they can be included in your payments.

chunks.title: What you need to do
chunks.text: You need to apply to keep these payments going. To apply, contact our International Services teamexternal at least 4 weeks before you leave NZ. You and your partner (if you have one) will need to provide: - your passport/s - another form of ID, and - your travel itinerary or tickets.

chunks.title: More information
chunks.text: More information about getting SLP or SPS in these countries can be found on our Social Security Agreementexternal pages.

chunks.title: Malta
chunks.text: Your benefit payment will stop. The Maltese Department of Social Security decides who can get a pension for retirement or widowhood and how much will be paid. You’ll need to contact them when you get to Malta. Visit the Department of Social Security – Malta websiteexternal

chunks.title: South Korea
chunks.text: Your benefit payment will stop. If you're 60 or older, you may be able to get the Korean Old Age benefit. This is paid by the South Korean National Pension Service in South Korea. They'll decide who can get this pension and how much you’ll be paid. If you want to apply for this pension, contact International Servicesexternal before you leave New Zealand.

chunks.title: United Kingdom
chunks.text: In most cases you can’t get any payments. You may be able to get payments from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) in the United Kingdom (UK). It depends what payments you're getting from us. If you're getting: - Jobseeker Support from us, you may be able to get Jobseeker's Allowance or Statutory Sick Pay from DWP. Statutory Sick Pay is paid for up to 28 weeks. - Supported Living Payment from us because you have a health condition, injury or disability, you may be able to get Employment and Support Allowance from DWP. - Sole Parent Support from us because you're a widow or widower, you may be able to get Widowed Parent's Allowance or Bereavement Allowance from DWP. The DWP in the UK decides who can get these payments and how much will be paid.

chunks.title: United Kingdom
chunks.text: If you want advice or guidance about what to do, you can contact International Servicesexternal. If you want to apply for a DWP payment, you need to contact the DWP. Visit DWP websiteexternal

chunks.title: Temporarily returning to NZ
chunks.text: If you're visiting New Zealand temporarily or on holiday, you can continue to get the same payments as you get when overseas.

chunks.title: Community Services Card
chunks.text: If you live overseas but are going to be temporarily in New Zealand, you may be able to get a temporary Community Services Card. This can help with the costs of health care and public transport while in New Zealand. There are certain criteria you need to meet. Call us on 0800 999 999 for more information. Community Services Cardexternal
