chunks.title: Payments to help you at work
chunks.text: We can help pay for things you need to do your job. These could be things like training, transport, gear and clothing, or help to keep your job. There's lots of things we can help pay for to make your job easier. These could be things you need when you start out, while you're working, or to support you if you're disabled or have a health condition.

chunks.title: Starting out
chunks.text: These things can help when you start your new job, or before you start.

chunks.title: Costs when you start work
chunks.text: A Transition to Work Grant can help you pay for things you need to find or start a job. These can be things like clothes, travel, living expenses until your first pay and other things. Transition to Work Grant

chunks.title: Getting to work
chunks.text: Help to get your driver licence, pay for public transport, or get repairs or modifications done on your car. Transport to work

chunks.title: Moving for a job
chunks.text: We may be able to help with travel and moving costs if you're relocating for a new job. Relocate for Work Support

chunks.title: While you're working
chunks.text: These things can help if you already have a job.

chunks.title: Need time off
chunks.text: A New Employment Transition Grant can help if you can’t go to work because you’re sick or can’t get your normal childcare. It can help if you have no sick or paid leave and you’ve recently stopped getting a benefit. New Employment Transition Grant

chunks.title: Training for your job
chunks.text: Skills for Industry can help you get on-the-job training and a qualification to advance in the industry. Skills for Industry

chunks.title: Help to pay your bills
chunks.text: We can help you pay an unexpected cost, or get your finances sorted, even if you've got a job. Help while you’re working

chunks.title: Help to keep your job
chunks.text: Flexi-wage is support for you and your employer if you need help to keep your job. We can help pay for training, help your employer avoid redundancies, or find a new job for you in the same business. Find out more about Flexi-wage

chunks.title: Seasonal work
chunks.text: You may be able to get help to pay for things like clothes, gear or temporarily moving home. There's also help if you can't work due to bad weather. Doing seasonal work

chunks.title: Health and disability assistance
chunks.text: These things can help if you’re disabled or have a health condition.

chunks.title: Need training or extra costs to do your job
chunks.text: We may be able to help if you're disabled or have a health condition and need training or have extra costs to do your job. Job and Training Support Funds

chunks.title: Vehicle modification
chunks.text: If you have a serious disability and need help to buy or modify a car or other vehicle, you may be able to get Vehicle Modification Funding. Vehicle Modification Funding

chunks.title: Payments when a client dies
chunks.text: If a client passes away, we may be able to keep their payments going for 28 days, or pay it into your account instead. When a client dies, we need to know. Please contact us. If they were getting NZ Super or Veteran's Pension you can tell us by filling out our online form. Contact us Register a senior's death with usexternal

chunks.title: Single clients with no dependent children
chunks.text: If the client who died was single and doesn't have any dependent children, we'll stop their payments as soon as we know they died. We may be able to keep making their payments for up to 28 days if: - their living situation means there are transition costs their family has to pay, causing hardship. For example, the client was sharing accommodation and the family has to pay household costs - there are exceptional and justified costs associated with their death. For example, multiple deaths within one family. A family member or the executor of the client's estate can ask us to do this.

chunks.title: How to ask us to keep making payments
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 (or 0800 552 002 if they're a senior client) and book an appointment to come in and see us. If you don't want to come by yourself, you can bring someone with you for support. You need to bring: - proof of who you are (unless you're already getting a payment from us) - confirmation of death, eg a death certificate (you can order this online here), or newspaper death notice - proof of the expenses that need to be paid. At the appointment, we'll: - ask you to fill in a Personal Declaration form - talk with you about anything else you could get, eg help with funeral costs.

chunks.title: Payments made after 28 days
chunks.text: We might not find out the client has died until after 28 days. In this case we may have to recover any payments we've made after the 28 days from their estate (if they have one).

chunks.title: If the client owed us money
chunks.text: Find out what happens if client had a debt with us, and what happens to that debt: Your debt with us

chunks.title: Single clients with dependent children
chunks.text: We'll keep paying the client for 28 days if the client who died was single and: - had a dependent child in their care, or - paid child support for a child, or - was getting Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit for a child in their care. If the client was paying child support through a private arrangement, we might not know about their child. In this case, we may not keep paying the client for 28 days. If you're now caring for the child, you can ask us to make their payments into your bank account instead. Unfortunately if we've already made payments into the client's account, we can't transfer these to you. You'll need to talk about this with the client's bank.

chunks.title: How to change the bank account
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 (or 0800 552 002 if they're a senior client) and book an appointment to come in and see us. You need to bring: - proof of who you are (unless you're already getting a payment from us) - confirmation of death, eg a death certificate (you can order this online), or newspaper death notice Death certificateexternal - proof that you're now caring for the child - evidence of your bank account number (unless we're already making payments for you into that bank account). At the appointment, we'll: - ask you to fill in a Personal Declaration form - talk with you about anything else you could get, eg an Orphan's Benefit or Unsupported Child's Benefit Orphan's Benefit Unsupported Child's Benefit

chunks.title: Payments made after 28 days
chunks.text: We might not find out the client has died until after 28 days. In this case we may have to recover any payments we've made after the 28 days from their estate (if they have one).

chunks.title: If the client owed us money
chunks.text: Find out what happens if client had a debt with us, and what happens to that debt: Your debt with us

chunks.title: Clients with a partner
chunks.text: If the client who died has a partner, we'll keep paying the client for 28 days. The only time we won't do this is if the partner gets a survivor's grant from ACC. However, the survivor's grant can take a while to be approved. If this happens, we can still make payments for 28 days but the partner will need to pay it back once ACC approve the grant. If you're the partner of the client who's died, you can ask us to make their payments into your bank account instead. Unfortunately, if we've already made payments into the client's account, we can't transfer these to you. You'll need to talk about this with the client's bank.

chunks.title: How to change the bank account
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 (or 0800 552 002 if they're a senior client) and book an appointment to come in and see us. If you don't want to come by yourself, you can bring someone with you for support. You need to bring: - proof of who you are (unless you're already getting a payment from us) - confirmation of death, eg a death certificate (you can order this online), or newspaper death notice Death certificateexternal - evidence of your bank account number (unless we're already making payments for you into that bank account). At the appointment, we'll: - ask you to fill in a Personal Declaration form - talk with you about anything else you could get, eg help with funeral costs. If you're already getting a benefit or payment from us, we'll review this at the appointment to make sure you're getting the right amount.

chunks.text: We might not find out the client has died until after 28 days. In this case we may have to recover any payments we've made after the 28 days from their estate (if they have one).

chunks.title: Pension or Superannuation scheme payments
chunks.text: If you get an overseas pension, regular or one-off payment from a superannuation scheme you need to tell us about it as it may affect your benefit. This does not include NZ Super.

chunks.title: What is this?
chunks.text: You need to tell us if you receive a regular payment from any pension or superannuation scheme as it will affect your benefit. This includes: - overseas pensions - New Zealand Government Superannuation schemes - other registered superannuation schemes. This does not include NZ Super payments.

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: You need to contact us. Phone us

chunks.title: Lump sum payment from a superannuation scheme
chunks.text: Your benefit won't be affected if your super scheme is registered and has a lock-in clause. The clause stops you accessing the money until you reach a certain age, or you leave the employer which set up the scheme. Once you access the money and use this to live on, your benefit will be affected. If you invest the money and earn interest, this will be counted as income and you have to tell us about it.

chunks.title: How your benefit will be affected
chunks.text: You can check how your income will affect your benefit using the income deduction tables. Income deduction tables

chunks.text: If you need help with ongoing phone costs that are directly related to your disability or health condition, we may be able to help you pay this as part of a Disability Allowance. - You can get a Disability Allowance for a number of different things, including phone costs. The maximum you can get for a Disability Allowance is $82.85 a week. - You don't have to be on a benefit to qualify for a Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You can apply for a Disability Allowance for you, your partner or a child. The person who needs help with phone costs must have: - a health condition or disability that's likely to last at least 6 months from when they were diagnosed - regular, ongoing costs because of the health condition or disability that are not fully covered by another agency - had a phone connected, or need to get a phone connected, because of a disability or health condition. To apply, you need to be: - 16 and older - a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident. It also depends on how much you and your partner earn.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: We pay up to a maximum of $82.85 a week for Disability Allowance. How much you get for phone costs depends on your situation. We may be able to pay for: - the regular and ongoing costs of renting a basic phone - phone line rental - wiring maintenance charges - the ongoing cost of a cell phone depending on your situation (for example you don't have a landline or there are no phone lines available).

chunks.title: We don't pay for:
chunks.text: - the cost of buying a phone - phone installation - extra costs, for example toll calls, call minder or call waiting (unless it's necessary and directly related to your disability).

chunks.title: Already getting payments from us (e.g. a benefit or Accommodation Supplement) but not Disability Allowance
chunks.text: - You need to complete the Disability Allowance application form and a health practitioner (e.g. your doctor) needs to complete the Disability Certificate inside. - Your health practitioner also needs to complete a Disability Certificate form. - You need to get a copy of your phone account or a quote from the phone company showing the line rental costs. - Call us on 0800 559 009 to talk to us about how to get these documents to us. chunks.text: - A health practitioner (e.g. your doctor) needs to complete a Disability Certificate form. - You need to get a copy of your phone account or a quote from the phone company showing the line rental costs. - Call us on 0800 559 009 to talk about your situation. We'll let you know if we need any other information and how to get this to us. Disability Certificate form (PDF 197 KB)

chunks.title: Power, gas and heating if you have a disability
chunks.text: If you have extra power, gas or heating costs because of your disability or health condition, we may be able to help you pay this as part of a Disability Allowance. - You can get a Disability Allowance for a number of different things, including power, gas and heating. The maximum you can get for a Disability Allowance is $82.85 a week. - You don't have to be on a benefit to qualify for a Disability Allowance.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You can apply for a Disability Allowance for you, your partner or a child. The person who needs help with their power, gas or heating costs must have: - a health condition or disability that's likely to last at least 6 months from when they were diagnosed - regular, ongoing costs because of the health condition or disability that are not fully covered by another agency - additional power, gas or heating costs because of the health condition or disability - power, gas and heating costs over and above normal usage. To apply, you need to be: - 16 and older, and - a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident. It also depends on how much you and your partner earn. The income limits for Disability Allowance are:

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: We pay up to a maximum of $82.85 a week for Disability Allowance. How much you get for power, gas and heating depends on your situation. We will pay for: - the portion of your power and gas costs over and above normal usage - the cost of firewood over and above normal usage if you use this method of heating. We'll include the cost of power, gas or heating from the date your Disability Allowance is granted.

chunks.text: - You need to complete the Disability Allowance application form, and a health practitioner (e.g. your doctor) needs to complete the Disability Certificate inside. - Your health practitioner also needs to complete a Disability Allowance medical certificate. - You need to get copies of: your power or gas accounts receipts for gas, coal or firewood - your power or gas accounts - receipts for gas, coal or firewood - Call us on 0800 559 009 we can talk with you about the best way to get these documents to us.

chunks.title: Drug testing
chunks.text: Information about drug testing and what it means when you're looking for work and getting a benefit. When you're on a benefit with an obligation to look for work, you have to take and pass any drug test potential employers or training providers require. If you don't do this, you may not meet your work obligations and your benefit could be reduced or stopped. This includes if: - a suitable job is available and you tell us you can't apply as you think you'll fail the drug test - you refuse to take the drug test for a suitable job or course, or - you fail the drug test for a suitable job or course you've been referred to.

chunks.title: When you have to take a drug test
chunks.text: You have to take a drug test if: - you apply for a job and an employer needs you to pass a pre-employment drug test as part of them employing you, or - you're doing employment-related training and the training provider uses drug tests as part of the admission process. For example, you need to do a drug test to get your heavy truck licence. In some circumstances we will not refer you to jobs that need a drug test. This includes if we know that you are: - dependent on, or addicted to, drugs - undergoing or waiting for drug addiction or dependence treatment, or - taking prescription medication that could cause you to fail a drug test.

chunks.title: Why employers do drug testing
chunks.text: Employers and training providers have to provide a safe working environment for their employees and students. This means drug testing may be necessary if an employee or student's ability to do their job can impact on the safety of themselves or others. Pre-employment drug tests are common in industries such as fishing, horticulture, transport and forestry.

chunks.title: How drug tests are done
chunks.text: We’ll tell you if the job or training course requires a drug test before we refer you to it. Your employer or training provider will organise the test for you. Tell us straight away if you think you may not pass the drug test. If you pass the test, you won’t need to pay for it.

chunks.title: Before you take the test
chunks.text: Before you take the drug test, the person overseeing the test will explain: - the type of test they’re using - how the test works, and - when you’ll know if you’ve passed or not.

chunks.title: Types of drug tests
chunks.text: Drug tests are completed under a national drug testing standard. There are 2 types of tests, both usually needing a urine sample: - a screening test, and - an evidential test. Most employers will only do the first screening test. This generally provides them with enough information to make a decision on whether to employ you or not.

chunks.title: Screening test
chunks.text: This is 98% accurate and shows within about 5 minutes if your urine has tested positive for drugs. It costs between $30 and $70. If you pass the drug test, you won’t need to pay for it.

chunks.title: Evidential test
chunks.text: This is 99.9% accurate and shows what type of drug and how much is in the sample. Your test sample would be sent away to a laboratory with the results being given to you some time later. It costs around $120. If you pass the drug test, you won’t need to pay for it.

chunks.title: Give a urine sample
chunks.text: You will usually give your urine sample in a specially prepared toilet area. This area is designed to ensure your privacy while keeping the sample safe from tampering or contamination. This will be done under strictly controlled conditions.

chunks.title: If you fail a drug test
chunks.text: If you fail a drug test, the person overseeing the test will: - discuss the result with you - ask you whether you accept the result, and confirm it if you do - ask you to sign a confirmation form agreeing to the result. If you don't agree with the result, talk to the person overseeing the test straight away. They may agree for you to do another test to confirm the result.

chunks.title: What happens to your benefit
chunks.text: What you'll need to do depends on how many times you've failed a drug test without a good reason. We will always tell you what you'll need to do before you have a test.

chunks.title: First time you fail a drug test
chunks.text: If it's the first time, then: - you'll have to pay us back for the cost of the failed drug test. This cost will be taken out of your benefit in weekly payments. - you'll have to agree to stop using drugs so you can pass another drug test in the future.

chunks.title: Second time you fail a drug test
chunks.text: If it's the second time, then you must pass a third drug test within 25 working days. - We'll talk to you about approved drug testing providers and you'll need to arrange the third drug test yourself. - You'll need to pay for the third test, regardless of whether you pass or fail it. We can help pay for your third test but you'll have to pay us back and it will be taken out of your benefit in weekly payments.

chunks.title: Third time you fail a drug test
chunks.text: If it's the third time, or you don't take and pass a drug test within 25 working days, then your benefit will: - be paid at 50% for 13 weeks if you have dependent children, or - stop for 13 weeks if you don't have dependent children. Your benefit may be restarted earlier than 13 weeks if: - you agree to take part in an approved activity for at least 6 weeks, and - you're still entitled to the benefit.

chunks.title: Prescriptions and health practitioner costs
chunks.text: If you have healthcare costs for you and your family, and you're on a benefit or a low income, we may be able to help.

chunks.title: Health practitioner fees
chunks.text: If you have to visit a health practitioner, for example a doctor, because of a health condition or disability you have that will last longer than 6 months, we may be able to help cover their fees with a Disability Allowance. Disability Allowance If you or a family member need to go to a health practitioner, for example a doctor, and you can't cover their fees, we may be able to help with a Special Needs Grant. Special Needs Grant

chunks.title: Prescription costs
chunks.text: If you have to pay for prescriptions because of a health condition or disability you have that will last longer than 6 months, we may be able to help cover them with the Disability Allowance. Disability Allowance If you or a family member can't cover your prescription costs, we may be able to help with a Special Needs Grant. Special Needs Grant If you and your family have received and been charged for 20 subsidised prescription items before the end of the pharmaceutical year (February 1 to January 31 the next year), you may be able to get free prescriptions for the rest of that year. It's easier to manage this if you go to one pharmacy.

chunks.title: Travel and accommodation costs
chunks.text: We may be able to help with the cost of travelling to your health practitioner, eg, your doctor. You don't have to be on a benefit to get this help. You won't have to pay the money back.

chunks.title: Children under 13
chunks.text: Children under 13 may be able to get free visits to their health practitioner, eg, their doctor, and may not be charged the standard $5 pharmacy charge for each prescription item.

chunks.title: Community Services Card
chunks.text: A Community Services Card can help with the costs of healthcare. You'll pay less for some health services simply by showing your card. Most people who are on a benefit automatically get one of these cards. If you're not on a benefit, you can apply for one.

chunks.title: Emergency medical treatment
chunks.text: We may be able to help with the cost of emergency medical treatment, eg doctor's fees, prescription charges or hospital care. Call us to discuss your situation. Phone us

chunks.title: Previous COVID-19 payments
chunks.text: Find information about previous payments that were available during COVID-19. This includes the COVID-19 Wage Subsidies, Income Relief Payment, Short-Term Absence Payment and Leave Support Scheme. During COVID-19 our role was to help employers and self-employed people so they could keep paying their staff and keep them in their jobs. We also helped people who lost their jobs due to COVID-19.

chunks.title: List of previous COVID-19 payments
chunks.text: COVID-19 Leave Support SchemeAvailable from 6 April 2020 (then called 'COVID-19 Essential Workers Leave Support Scheme') until 15 August 2023. It was to help employers, and self-employed people, pay employees who had to self-isolate due to COVID-19. COVID-19 Short-Term Absence PaymentAvailable from 9 February 2021 to 17 October 2022. It was to help businesses pay their employees while they waited for PCR test results. COVID-19 Wage Subsidies August 2021Available from 20 August 2021 to 9 December 2021. These were a series of 9 payments to help businesses pay staff and protect jobs affected by the alert level changes on 17 August 2021. COVID-19 Wage Subsidy March 2021Available from 4 March 2021 to 21 March 2021. It was to help businesses pay staff impacted by the alert level changes on 28 February 2021.

chunks.title: List of previous COVID-19 payments
chunks.text: COVID-19 Resurgence Wage SubsidyAvailable from 21 August 2020 to 3 September 2020. It was to help businesses who had a decline in revenue keep paying their staff. COVID-19 Income Relief PaymentAvailable from 8 June 2020 to 14 November 2020. It was to help people who lost their jobs because of COVID-19. COVID-19 Wage Subsidy ExtensionAvailable from 10 June 2020 to 1 September 2020. It was to help businesses who had a decline in revenue keep paying their staff. 2020 COVID-19 Wage SubsidyAvailable from 17 March 2020 to 9 June 2020. It was to help businesses who had a decline in revenue keep paying their staff. COVID-19 Leave paymentAvailable from 17 March 2020 to 27 March 2020. It was to help businesses keep paying their staff who could not work because they were in self-isolation.

chunks.title: Obligations and repayments
chunks.text: All COVID-19 payments had obligations which employers and self-employed people who applied were required to meet. These obligations included: - paying their employees correctly - keeping their employees in their jobs - keeping evidence to show they were eligible for the payment - following employment law - repaying the payment if they were no longer entitled to it. The full eligibility and obligations details are listed in the declarations of each payment. If a business does not meet these obligations, or no longer meets the criteria, they may need to repay the COVID-19 payment. Find out when a business needs to repay this and how to repay it: Repaying a COVID-19 payment

chunks.title: Businesses that received a Wage Subsidy
chunks.text: You can search on the Ministry of Social Development (MSD) website to see which businesses were paid a COVID-19 Wage Subsidy. The search will tell you: - the name of the business - the number of employees they were paid for - the amount paid. Wage Subsidy Employer Search (Ministry of Social Development)external

chunks.title: Information for employees
chunks.text: Only employers or self-employed people could make an application for a COVID-19 payment. This means your employer had to apply for you, you could not make an application for yourself. Your employer must have told you they were applying for you before they applied. They must also have had your consent to share some of your details with us. They must have declared they did this when they applied. Your employer can't change your employment agreement unless you agree to the change first. Your employer still has to follow your employment agreement during COVID-19, including how much you get paid. Talk to your employer if you have questions about whether they got a COVID-19 payment for you, or how this was paid.

chunks.title: Information for employees
chunks.text: You can also find information on the Employment New Zealand website: Employment New Zealandexternal

chunks.title: Released from prison
chunks.text: If you've been released from prison or are no longer being held in remand, we may be able to help you in a number of ways. It's important you contact us right away as there may be a stand-down period before you get the first payment of any benefit.

chunks.title: Help to get set up in the community
chunks.text: You may be able to get a Steps to Freedom grant if you've been in prison or remand for 31 days or more. It can help with initial set up costs, eg: - housing - living expenses, eg power, a phone connection or food - other essential costs, eg bedding, clothing, appliances or toiletry items. Steps to Freedom grant

chunks.text: You're looking for full-time work and need help with day-to-day living expenses until you find a job. Jobseeker Support When you apply for Jobseeker Support, there may be some things you need to do before you can get it. Online application process

chunks.title: Ability to work affected because of a health condition or disability

chunks.title: Problems with your payment card
chunks.text: What to do if your card locks, declines, or you have any other problems with your payment card.

chunks.title: Incorrect PIN
chunks.text: You need to set a personalised PIN to use your payment card. If you haven't set your own PIN the card won't work. If you have more than one card, you need to set a PIN for each card.

chunks.title: How to set your PIN:
chunks.text: - Log in to MyMSDexternal. - Go to 'My payment cards'. - Select the card you want to add a PIN for. - Enter a 4-digit PIN - don't use a PIN that is consecutive, easily associated with you (like birthdays), or the numbers on your card. - Re-enter your PIN to confirm. - Done! Your PIN is now ready to go. Other ways to set your PIN: - Call us and say "set my card PIN" - register your voice so you can set your PIN by calling us at any time without waiting to talk to a person - our staff in our service centres can help set your PIN in MyMSD - we have other ways you can contact us if you're deaf, hard of hearing or have a speech impairment.

chunks.title: Reset your PIN
chunks.text: You can reset your PIN by following the same steps above.

chunks.title: Locked card
chunks.text: The card will lock if you enter an incorrect PIN 5 times. You can unlock this by resetting your PIN, or wait until the next day – the card will unlock automatically at midnight.

chunks.title: EFTPOS issues
chunks.text: Here's what you need to do if you have problems at the EFTPOS machine: The transaction may also be declined if the: - money on the card has expired: The money will only stay on the payment card for 7 days. After that it expires. You can check the expiry date in MyMSD. If you still need the money, call us and say 'Payment card' when you're asked why you're calling. - amount you're charged is more than the amount on the card: You need to reduce the amount being spent. - shop is not registered with us: Shops need to be registered to accept our payment cards in their EFTPOS machines. - signature does not match: The signature on the back of your card must match your signature on the receipt. No one else can use your card on your behalf.

chunks.title: Checking your payment
chunks.text: You can go online and use MyMSD to check: - the balance on your card - your previous transactions - when your payment expires. Log into MyMSD, or find out how to get a MyMSD account. My MSD About MyMSD

chunks.title: Lost, stolen or damaged cards
chunks.text: Call us if: - you can't find your card (if you think it's lost or stolen) - you think someone else is using your card without your permission - your card is broken or damaged. Say 'Payment Card' when you are asked to say why you're calling. Phone us

chunks.title: Cancelled and expired cards
chunks.text: Your payment card may be cancelled if it has been damaged or lost. Once a card is cancelled it can no longer be used. Payment cards will also expire after a set amount of time, and once it expires it can no longer be used. You can find your card's expiry date in 'My payment cards' in MyMSD. If you need a new card you can find out how to get one here: Getting a payment card

chunks.title: Refunds
chunks.text: If you get a refund this will be credited against any debts you have with us. If you still need money to get the item you returned, talk to us.

chunks.title: Registered suppliers who can't accept payment cards
chunks.text: Sometimes suppliers who are registered with us can't accept our payment cards. This could be because: - they don't use EFTPOS - the EFTPOS network or our internal systems are down - there's a state of emergency or natural disaster. When you call us to apply, we'll talk about whether your supplier can accept payment cards, and other ways we can help if they can't.

chunks.title: Professional clothing and career advice for men
chunks.text: Support and practical help for men looking for work. You can get professional work clothing, career development tools and an ongoing support network. It's available in Northland, Wellington and Bay of Plenty. This service helps men find economic independence. They can help you get ready for job interviews, and support you when you're starting a new job.

chunks.title: What is this service
chunks.text: This is a 3-part service:

chunks.title: Clothes for work
chunks.text: You'll get the right clothing and footwear for your job interview, and another outfit suitable for your first week of work. This is a one-on-one service designed to meet your needs and the type of job you're looking for.

chunks.title: Careers services
chunks.text: Practical skills and advice to boost your chances of getting and keeping a job. You'll get help to prepare your CV, improve your skills for job interviews, and learn how to plan your career. This might be one-on-one or in group workshops.

chunks.title: Ongoing support
chunks.text: Once you're in work, you can access other services like mentoring programmes, buddy systems or networks. These will help you take the next step in your career.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: To get this you need to qualify for a Transition to Work Grant from us. This covers the cost of the service. Check the Transition to Work Grant page on our website to find out who can get this and how to apply: Transition to work grant

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 to apply for a Transition to Work Grant. We'll talk with you to understand your situation and how we can help. We'll let you know what information you need to provide and how to get this to us.

chunks.title: How to contact the service
chunks.text: This service is run by Dress for Success. You can call the Dress for Success offices below to get more information, make a booking, or to ask any questions. Northland: 09 4385505 Bay of Plenty: 07 348 3660 Wellington: 04 473 2940

chunks.title: Public transport fares
chunks.text: You can get a 50% discount on single-trip adult fares on public transport if you have a Community Services Card. This discount is part of the Community Connect programme. You need to apply for the discount through your local transport provider. Check with your local public transport provider what discounts are available and which ones are the best for you.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You can get the Community Connect discount if you have a Community Services Card (CSC). More information on who can get a CSC is on our page:

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: First, you need to apply for a Community Services Card if you don't already have one. Once you have a Community Services Card, you can apply for the Community Connect discount through your local transport provider. Visit your local transport provider's website to find out how to apply. We've listed some of them in the table below. You can get a free travel card when you apply for Community Connect. You may need to load a minimum of $5 onto the new card. Check with your local transport provider for more information.

chunks.title: SuperGold card and the Community Services Card
chunks.text: If you have a SuperGold card you can already travel for free on public transport at off-peak times. If you have a Community Services Card (CSC) as well as a SuperGold card, or a combo card, you can apply for a 50% discount at peak travel-times as well. SuperGold Card In most cases, you need one travel card for each discount. If you want discounted travel during on- and off-peak times, you may need two travel cards.You could have the: - SuperGold discount, for free off-peak travel on one card, and - Community Connect discount on a second travel card. See your local public transport provider’s website for more information and how to apply.

chunks.title: Reapply for Temporary Additional Support (TAS)
chunks.text: If you're getting Temporary Additional Support and you still need it after 13 weeks, you have to re-apply. You need to do this before your payment stops.

chunks.title: Who can reapply
chunks.text: You can reapply for Temporary Additional Support if you still meet the criteria. Temporary Additional Support You must also have taken: - all necessary steps to try and pay your expenses another way, e.g.: if your circumstances have changed, use our 'Check what you might get' tool to see if there's any other payments you could get if you're working, check if you can get Working for Families payments from Inland Revenue - if your circumstances have changed, use our 'Check what you might get' tool to see if there's any other payments you could get - if you're working, check if you can get Working for Families payments from Inland Revenue - reasonable steps to increase your income and reduce your costs, e.g.: getting budgeting advice stopping paid subscriptions, e.g. Netflix, Sky, Spotify looking for paid work or increasing your hours of work.

chunks.title: Who can reapply
chunks.text: - getting budgeting advice - stopping paid subscriptions, e.g. Netflix, Sky, Spotify - looking for paid work or increasing your hours of work.

chunks.title: How to reapply
chunks.text: You'll get a letter (with a re-application form), as well as a notification in MyMSD, at least 4 weeks before you need to re-apply for Temporary Additional Support. You need to re-apply before your Temporary Additional Support stops. If you don't, we can only start it again from the date you re-apply. This may mean you have a gap in your payments.

chunks.title: Reapply in MyMSD
chunks.text: To re-apply in MyMSD you need to: - log in to MyMSD - select re-apply - complete the online form - upload any documents, if required - submit the online form. If there's been a change to your partner or child details, you'll need to talk with us. MyMSD will let you know if you need to do this. myMSD login

chunks.title: Can't use MyMSD
chunks.text: If you can't use MyMSD, you can either: - call us and say "Temporary Additional Support" and we may be able to help you re-apply over the phone, or - complete the re-application form we sent you and drop it off to your local service centre We'll let you know if there are any documents you need to provide. You'll need to drop these off to your local service centre. Local service centre

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: Once your online form has been processed, we'll send you a letter to let you know the outcome.

chunks.title: Re-establishment grant
chunks.text: The Re-establishment grant is a payment to help people in specific circumstances re-establish themselves in the community. A re-establishment grant can pay for things like: - accommodation, including bond and rent in advance - beds, bedding and essential appliances - a fridge, freezer or washing machine - connecting electricity, gas and telephone - clothing - cost of attending English language classes, including transport costs - translation costs for work-related documents.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You must meet the qualifications for a Special Needs Grant. If you're an Afghan evacuee and have an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa, you don't need to meet the residency criteria for a Special Needs Grant. You also need to be re-establishing yourself in the community and be in one of the following situations: - you're a refugee who isn't entitled to other forms of government assistance for refugees - you're a sole parent who: is a victim of family violence is being assisted by a social service agency (e.g. Women's Refuge) to relocate after the initial separation, and has no other resources - is a victim of family violence - is being assisted by a social service agency (e.g. Women's Refuge) to relocate after the initial separation, and

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: - has no other resources - you're a patient in hospital or a residential home for more than 6 months - you've just been released from a custody period of 31 days or more - you're an Afghan interpreter who has a residence class visa - you're an Afghan evacuee who either: is a New Zealand citizen has a residence class visa (including an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa), or has applied for an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa, or - is a New Zealand citizen - has a residence class visa (including an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa), or - has applied for an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Visa, or - you're in a 'Transition from Care to Independence' initiative with Oranga Tamariki and: 16 or older have been in supported care under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 leaving supported care to live independently have a letter from your personal advisor verifying that you're participating in this initiative and have a youth transition payment.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: - 16 or older - have been in supported care under the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989 - leaving supported care to live independently - have a letter from your personal advisor verifying that you're participating in this initiative and - have a youth transition payment. Re-establishment grants are considered on a case-by-case basis.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: How much you get depends on your situation.

chunks.title: Sole parent and victim of family violence
chunks.text: You can get up to $800 for accommodation costs but you have to pay this back. You can get up to $600 for other costs and you don't have to pay this back.

chunks.title: Long-term hospital or residential home
chunks.text: You can get up to $800 for accommodation costs but you have to pay this back. You can get up to $1,200 for other costs and you don't have to pay this back.

chunks.title: Refugee, Afghan interpreter or Afghan evacuee
chunks.text: You can get up to a total of $5,000. Of that $5,000, you can get up to $3,500 for accommodation costs. You don't have to pay back any of the $5,000.

chunks.title: Released from custody
chunks.text: You can get up to $350 for all costs and you don't have to pay this back.

chunks.title: Transition from care to independence initiative
chunks.text: You can get up to $800 for accommodation costs but you have to pay this back. You can get up to $1,200 for other costs and you don't have to pay this back.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You need to call us on 0800 559 009. We'll talk with you to understand your situation and how we can help. We'll let you know what information you need to provide and how to get this to us.

chunks.title: You're a refugee, Aghan interpreter or Afghan evacuee
chunks.text: You need to apply within the first year of your arrival in New Zealand. If you're applying for help with English language classes, you can apply within the first 2 years of your arrival in NZ.

chunks.title: Using NZ Realm countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. If you haven't, you may be able to use time you've lived in NZ Realm countries to meet this criteria. NZ Realm countries are the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau.

chunks.title: Residence criteria
chunks.text: You must have lived in NZ for a certain number of years from age 20. This must include 5 years from age 50. The total number of years you need is based on your date of birth. If you're a refugee or protected person, this may be different depending on the age you started living in NZ. These years (including the 5 years from age 50) do not need to be consecutive. Work out how many years you need

chunks.title: Residence criteria in other languages
chunks.text: You can read the residence criteria in Cook Island Māori, Niuean or Tokelauan. Residence criteria in other languages

chunks.title: Using a NZ Realm country to meet residence criteria
chunks.text: Of the total number of years, you need to have lived in NZ for at least 10 years from age 20. For the rest of the years, you can include time you've spent living in NZ, the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau (or a combination of these). When we say 'have lived in a NZ realm country', we mean you were 'resident' and 'physically present' in the realm country at the same time.

chunks.title: How to meet the residence criteria
chunks.text: Add together your time in: - NZ from age 20 (must be at least 10 years), and - the NZ Realm country (or countries) from age 20. This needs to add up to the total number of years you need to meet the residence criteria. The total must include 5 years from age 50 (you can use your time in the NZ Realm country, or countries, for the 5 years too). If you want to talk about your situation, contact our International Services team. International Services

chunks.title: If you don't meet residence criteria using NZ Realm countries
chunks.text: You may have spent time living in, or contributing to the pension scheme of, a Social Security Agreement (SSA) country. If so, you may be able to use this time to meet the residence criteria as well. If you're ordinarily resident in a NZ Realm country when you apply for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension, you usually cannot use time from an SSA country. You may be able to use time from some SSA countries (Australia, Canada, Denmark, Ireland, Malta and the Netherlands) if you meet certain criteria. If you want to talk about your situation, contact our International Services team. Contact International Services team Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super

chunks.title: Resident in a realm country
chunks.text: Being resident in a realm country means you permanently made your home in the realm country. In most cases, you'll be resident in a realm country if you lived there on a permanent basis for the required number of years. In other cases, we may need to consider other things to work out if you've been resident in a realm country. To do this, we'll look at your involvement in the realm country's society, e.g. your: - employment - community activities - club memberships, and - local churches.

chunks.title: Physically present in a realm country
chunks.text: To work this out, we'll look at if you were physically in the realm country for the required number of years. If you left the realm country, you weren't physically present in that realm country for that period of time. For example, if you went on holiday for: - 25 days, you weren't physically present in the realm country for 25 days. This means you would need to have lived in the realm country for an extra 25 days to make up what is required - 14 days every year for 10 years, that's 140 days in total. This means you weren't physically present in the realm country for 140 days. So you would need to have lived in the realm country for an extra 140 days to make up what is required.

chunks.title: Examples
chunks.text: You were born in NZ on 12 May 1978. At age 25 you moved to the Cook Islands and you still live there. You apply for NZ Super (from the Cook Islands) when you turn 65. Based on your date of birth, you must have lived in NZ for at least 20 years from age 20. The 20 years must include 5 years from age 50. To meet the residence criteria, you can use the time you've lived in the Cook Islands. Of the 20 years, you must have lived: - at least 10 years in NZ, and - the rest of the years in NZ or the Cook Islands. In this example, you have: - 5 years living in NZ from age 20-25 - 40 years living in the Cook Islands from age 25-65. You would not meet the residence criteria as you have only lived in NZ for 5 years from age 20.

chunks.title: Examples
chunks.text: You were born in NZ on 12 May 1963. You moved to Tokelau at age 30. You move back to NZ at age 65 and apply for NZ Super. Based on your date of birth, you must have lived in NZ for at least 12 years from age 20. The 12 years must include 5 years from age 50. To meet the residence criteria, you can use the time you've lived in Tokelau. Of the 12 years you must have lived: - at least 10 years in NZ - the rest of the years in NZ or Tokelau. In this example, you have: - 10 years living in NZ from age 20-30, and - 35 years living in Tokelau from age 30-65. This means you meet the residence criteria for NZ Super because you have: - 10 years living in NZ and - the rest of the years living in Tokelau. This includes the 5 years over 50.

chunks.title: Examples
chunks.text: You were born in NZ on 1 February 1979. You moved to Niue at age 60. You apply for NZ Super from Niue when you turn 65. Based on your date of birth, you must have lived in NZ for at least 20 years from age 20. The 20 years must include 5 years from age 50. To meet the residence criteria, you can use the time you've lived in Niue. These 20 years must be made up of: - at least 10 years living in NZ - the other 10 years living in NZ or Niue. In this example, you have: - 40 years living in NZ from age 20-60, and - 5 years living in Niue from age 60-65. This means you meet the residence criteria for NZ Super because you have: - 10 years living in NZ and - the rest of the years living in NZ and Niue. This includes the 5 years over 50.

chunks.title: Recoverable Assistance Payment
chunks.text: A Recoverable Assistance Payment is a one-off payment to help you pay an essential or emergency cost if you can't pay it another way. You don't qualify for this payment if you're on a benefit. You have to pay the money back.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may be able to get a Recoverable Assistance Payment if you: - don't get a benefit from us - have an essential or emergency cost you can't pay for - have no other way to pay for this cost - are either a: New Zealand citizen or permanent resident - New Zealand citizen or - permanent resident - normally live in New Zealand and intend to stay here. It also depends on: - how much you and your partner earn - any money or assets you and your partner have.

chunks.title: Current income limits
chunks.text: Single and 16 to 17 years old $45,716.84 Single and 18 years old or over $52,541.32 Couple (with or without children) $76,315.72 Sole parent with 1 child $63,756.68 Sole parent with 2 or more children $67,171

chunks.title: Asset limits
chunks.text: These don't include the things you need for day-to-day living, e.g. your home, car, and some payments after a severe weather event. They do include things like money in the bank, or a second property.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: How much you get depends on your situation and what you need help with. Examples of costs we can help with are: - ambulance subscription fees - attendance at funerals and tangihanga - beds, chairs and tables - car repairs - child car seat - clothing - costs to end your tenancy early, or sublet or assign your tenancy - dentures and hearing aids - driver licence - electricity, gas or water - fire loss or burglary - fridges, freezes and washing machines - glasses - school costs - school stationery - school uniforms - tenancy tribunal fees - travel if you're stranded. We may be able to help with other costs, it depends on your situation. If you're not sure whether we can help, talk with us about your situation.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You need to call us on 0800 559 009 We'll talk with you to understand your situation and how we can help. We'll let you know what information you need to provide and how to get this to us.

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: If your application is approved, we'll give you a payment card (if you don't already have one) and load the money onto it. We'll talk to you about how to get this to you. You have 7 days to spend the money before it expires.

chunks.title: Using your payment card
chunks.text: A payment card is like an Eftpos card and you can use it at any supermarket or store that accepts them. Information about Payment Cards You can login to MyMSD to see how much you have left on your payment card and when it expires. Find out more about MyMSD Once you've used your payment card, keep it. You can use it again if you need help from us in the future.

chunks.title: Refugees or protected persons residence criteria to get NZ Super and Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for a certain amount of time to get NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Find out how we work this out if you're recognised as a refugee or protected person. You must have lived in NZ for a certain number of years from age 20. This must include 5 years from age 50. These years (including the 5 years from age 50) do not need to be consecutive.

chunks.title: Find out how many years you need
chunks.text: Select the age you were when you started living in NZ to find out how many years you need. In each of these situations, you still need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 5 years since you turned 50. If you want to talk about your situation, contact our International Services team. International Services

chunks.title: Before age 45
chunks.text: How many years you need is based on your date of birth. Use the table on the 'Who can get NZ Super' page to find out how many years you need based on your date of birth. Who can get NZ Super

chunks.title: Example - started living in New Zealand at age 40
chunks.text: You started living in New Zealand as a refugee at age 40. You apply for NZ Super when you turn 65. You were born on 15 February 1980 so you must have lived in New Zealand for at least 20 years. The 20 years must include 5 years since you turned 50. You have lived in New Zealand for 25 years, including 5 years since you turned 50. This means you meet the residence criteria for NZ Super.

chunks.title: From age 45 to 54
chunks.text: You need the shorter time of either: - the number of years between when you started living in New Zealand and your 65th birthday, or - between 10 and 20 years - use the table on the 'Who can get NZ Super' page to find out how many years you need based on your date of birth. Who can get NZ Super

chunks.title: Example - started living in New Zealand at age 50
chunks.text: You started living in New Zealand as a refugee at age 50. You apply for NZ Super when you turn 65. Your date of birth is 10 September 1978. The total number of years you must have lived in New Zealand is the shorter time of either: - the 15 years between when you started living in New Zealand and your 65th birthday, or - 20 years (based on your date of birth). The shorter of these is 15 years, so this is the number of years you would need. The 15 years must include 5 years since you turned 50. This means you would meet the residence criteria for NZ Super.

chunks.title: From age 55
chunks.text: You need to have lived in New Zealand for at least 10 years.

chunks.title: Example - started living in New Zealand at age 60
chunks.text: You started living in New Zealand as a refugee at age 60. You apply for NZ Super when you turn 65. You've only lived in New Zealand for 5 years, from 60-65. This means you won't meet the residence criteria for NZ Super until you turn 70.

chunks.title: Don't meet the required years
chunks.text: You may be able to use other countries to meet this residence criteria if: - they are a country that has a Social Security Agreement with New Zealand, or - they are a New Zealand realm country (the Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau). Using SSA countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super Using NZ Realm countries to meet residence criteria for NZ Super

chunks.text: If your relationship status changes you must tell us right away as it could affect how much you're paid.

chunks.title: Relocate for Work Support
chunks.text: We may be able to help with travel and moving costs if you're relocating for a new job. You must apply for this payment before you move for your new job.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You need to meet the criteria below for: - yourself, and - your new job.

chunks.title: Criteria for yourself
chunks.text: You must: - be getting a main benefit (e.g. Jobseeker Support) - agree to cancel your main benefit from when you start your new job - be aged either: 8-64 years old, or 65 or older and don't qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension - 8-64 years old, or - 65 or older and don't qualify for NZ Super or Veteran's Pension - be likely to need a main benefit for a long time if you don't get this job - have organised a new place to live near your new job that's suitable for you and your family - have been unable to get a job in your current location - have not received any other payments from us for relocating for the same job, and - have applied for this payment before moving for your new job. We'll also look at:

chunks.title: Criteria for yourself
chunks.text: - any cash assets you or your partner have - whether you or your partner have been paid 'Relocate for Work Support' or '$5k to Work' in the last 52 weeks.

chunks.title: Criteria for your new job
chunks.text: You must have accepted an offer for a job in New Zealand, which must: - be either: 30 hours or more a week, or less than 30 hours a week if your pay is at least the same as 30 hours a week at minimum wage, or 20 hours a week if you're a sole parent and you only have part-time work obligations - 30 hours or more a week, or - less than 30 hours a week if your pay is at least the same as 30 hours a week at minimum wage, or - 20 hours a week if you're a sole parent and you only have part-time work obligations - pay at least minimum wage - be permanent, or fixed term, for at least 12 months - be too far away to commute from where you live now, and - be suitable for your skills, abilities and situation.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: Relocate for Work can help to pay towards: - travel expenses, and - the cost of moving your possessions, if needed. For example, you need to hire a truck or trailer because you can't fit them in your car.

chunks.title: Travel expenses
chunks.text: The maximum amount you can get depends on the method of transport and how many people in your family are moving. - If you're travelling by land, and air or sea, you will only get the amount for air or sea. - If you're travelling by one method and your family is travelling by another, you will only get the amount for air or sea.

chunks.title: Moving your possessions
chunks.text: You can only get this cost if you need it. The maximum amount you can get depends on how far you're moving and how many people in your family are moving.

chunks.title: Step 1 - Complete the application form
chunks.text: You need to complete the PDF application form. You can download and print it. If you can't print it, you can call us to get one posted to you, or you can pick up one from our service centres. Alternatively, you can arrive early for your appointment (see step 3) to complete the form in the service centre.

chunks.title: Step 2 - Gather your documents
chunks.text: You need to bring to your appointment: - proof of your new job offer, with the start date, number of hours, and duration of the contract - proof of what you did to try find work in your current area, e.g. job applications submitted or rejection letters, and - proof you have new accommodation arranged, e.g. a tenancy agreement or confirmation from family or friends you'll be staying with them.

chunks.title: Step 3 - Call us to book an appointment
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 to book an appointment at your local service centre.

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: We’ll usually grant or decline your application at your appointment. If your application's approved, we'll pay the money into your bank account. You may need to pay the money back if one of these things happens (unless there's a good reason): - you don't use the money for what it's intended for - you don't relocate within 28 days of getting the payment, or - you re-apply for a main benefit or Student Allowance within 6 months (182 days) of the date you're due to start your new job.

chunks.title: Renew your medical certificate or information
chunks.text: You may need to renew your medical certificate or medical information at certain times. It depends what payment you get as to what you have to do.

chunks.title: Jobseeker Support
chunks.text: If you have a health condition, injury or disability that impacts your ability to work, you would have provided a medical certificate. The medical certificate will show your medical coverage. This is a period of time where your health practitioner has determined that you can't work due to your health condition, injury or disability.

chunks.title: Medical coverage is due to expire
chunks.text: If your medical coverage is due to expire while you're getting Jobseeker Support, you'll need to provide another medical certificate. We'll write to you 4 weeks before your coverage expires asking you to either: - renew your medical certificate, or - tell us you're ready to look for work. If you're going to renew your medical certificate, you must do this before your medical coverage expires. If you can't renew it before the expiry date, contact us as soon as you can.

chunks.title: Find out when your medical coverage expires
chunks.text: You can use MyMSD to find out when your medical coverage expires. It's listed in the 'My Profile' section. You can also call us on 0800 559 009. MyMSD

chunks.title: Supported Living Payment
chunks.text: When you applied, you would have provided information that confirms your condition and the impact it has on your ability to work. Every 2 years we may ask you for updated medical information. We may ask for this even if your health condition or disability is permanent or hasn’t changed. This is to check how your health condition or disability currently impacts on your capacity to work. This will help us understand what support you need from us, and whether you’re able to work right now or in the future.

chunks.title: If you need to complete a review
chunks.text: We’ll write to you if you need to complete a Supported Living Payment review. We’ll ask you to show us a recently completed Work Capacity Medical Certificate completed by a health practitioner. If we need further information, we’ll let you know. If you can’t provide this information, or you want to see one of our designated doctors, call us to let us know.

chunks.title: Situations when you won't need to complete a review
chunks.text: We won't ask you to complete a Supported Living Payment review if you: - are totally blind - are terminally ill - have a severe intellectual or cognitive impairment - have a disorder that severely impacts on your ability to function and care for yourself and is unlikely to improve. How to tell us if something changes

chunks.title: Disability Allowance
chunks.text: You would have provided a Disability Certificate when you applied for Disability Allowance. The Disability Certificate shows the expected duration of the disability. This is how long your health practitioner has determined that you may have the disability for. Once you're getting a Disability Allowance, we may do a full review of this payment if: - your Disability Allowance has not been reviewed in the last 44 weeks or, - your medical condition or disability is due for reassessment. If we do a full review, we'll send you a 'Confirming your Circumstances' form. You have 25 working days to complete and sign the form and provide any relevant verification. This may include a Disability Certificate which you need to get your health practitioner to complete.

chunks.title: If the review is for your child
chunks.text: If the review is for your child, you'll need to get their health practitioner to complete the Disability Certificate. If you're also getting Child Disability Allowance for your child, this will be a separate review.

chunks.title: Child Disability Allowance
chunks.text: When you applied, your child's health practitioner would have completed a Medical Certificate. They would have let us know on the Medical Certificate when they think the child should next be reassessed for the Child Disability Allowance. We'll send you a letter 6 weeks before the reassessment date and then we'll send you a medical review form. You'll need to get the child's health practitioner to complete the medical review form. Then you'll need to send this back to us.

chunks.title: Rental income
chunks.text: You need to let us know if you get any type of rental income. This could be from someone renting a room, whole house, self-contained property or a non-accommodation property. If you don't tell us about rental income we may not pay you enough, or we may pay you too much and you'll have to pay the debt back.

chunks.title: What is rent
chunks.text: A renter is someone whose accommodation costs cover the room or property they stay in or use. This may also include services costs (e.g. gardening).

chunks.title: How much of your rent payments count as income
chunks.text: How much of a rent payment counts as income depends on the type of rent you're being paid for.

chunks.title: Rent payments from someone who lives with you
chunks.text: If someone lives with you and is paying you rent, we work out the income from this by: - looking at how much rent you are paid - comparing this to your accommodation costs If the rent payment is higher than your accommodation costs, we work out the difference – that difference counts as income. If the rent payment is lower than your accommodation costs, the rent payment does not count as income. However, it will affect the amount of any housing subsidy you get from us.

chunks.title: Rent payments for a property you don't live in
chunks.text: If someone is renting a property from you that you own but do not live in, some of the rent money can be used for certain expenses without it affecting your benefit. These expenses include: - interest payments earned on the money borrowed to buy the property - rates - house insurance - fees and commission if a property manager or agent is used - repairs and maintenance - other fees e.g. bank administration fees for the mortgage, tenancy agreement costs, any valuation required by your bank, accounting fees. Any rent payments you receive after these costs are paid is considered income.

chunks.title: Rent payments for a self-contained part of the property
chunks.text: If the self-contained part of the property is a granny flat or unit, it must have a kitchen or kitchenette and a bathroom. If it's a mobile home it needs to have facilities for: - day-to-day living - sleeping - preparing and cooking food. It must also have a: - sink - toilet - fresh water tank - waste water tank. To work out how much of the self-contained property's rent payments count as income, we: - look at the accommodation costs for the whole property - look at what proportion of the whole property is self-contained, to work out the percentage that you live in - reduce the accommodation costs for the whole property to the percentage that is self-contained - the final amount is your personal accommodation costs.

chunks.title: Rent payments for a self-contained part of the property
chunks.text: If that final amount is lower than the rent payment for the self-contained dwelling, these rent payments do not count as income. If that final amount is higher than the rent payment for the self-contained dwelling, we work out the difference – that difference counts as income.

chunks.title: Rent payments for non-accommodation property
chunks.text: Non-accommodation property is when someone rents an area of your property, but they do not live there, e.g. a garage used for storage. All the rent payment you receive for this type of rent is considered income.

chunks.title: How your benefit will be affected
chunks.text: You can check how your income will affect your benefit using the income deduction tables. Income deduction tables

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: The easiest way to tell us is online in MyMSD. Once you've logged in, select: - 'Declare boarders and renters' to let us know about rent payments from people who live with you, or - 'Declare wages' to let us know about any other payments you get for a rental property. When you 'Declare boarders and renters' in MyMSD, you need to tell us: - the address - details of the person paying you rent - how much the rent is - when you get paid, and how often. We will continue to use this amount every week, so make sure you let us know if it stops or changes. If you can't use MyMSD to tell us about renters who live with you, you can also fill out our PDF form: You need to print this form, complete it, and either post it to us or bring it into one of our services centres. You can also pick one up from any of our service centres.

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: Find a service centre If you need to tell us about other payments you get for a rental property and you can't use MyMSD, you can call us. Phone us

chunks.title: Repaying debt if you're not getting a benefit or pension
chunks.text: If you're not getting a main benefit, NZ Super, Veteran's Pension, or Accommodation Supplement you can set up a repayment arrangement to pay off your debt. We can work with you on a repayment plan that suits you. Go to the page 'Your debt with us' if you want information about: - how to get a breakdown of your debt - what to do if you don't agree with your debt - support for managing your debt - if someone has died and had a debt with us. Your debt with us

chunks.title: Debt repayment information
chunks.text: If you're getting a main benefit, NZ Super, Veteran's Pension or Accommodation Supplement, there's a different process for your debt repayments. What we mean by 'main benefit' Repaying debt while getting a benefit or pension

chunks.title: Help with your debt
chunks.text: If you need help with your debt or want to talk about it, you can contact our Client Support Debt Management team. Phone us

chunks.title: Debt repayment amount
chunks.text: Below is a guide of how much you could repay. This is just a guide, it depends how much you can afford. When deciding how much your repayments should be, you'll need to think of things like: - your budget - your upcoming expenses - any other debts you may have - how long you want to be repaying the money. You need to contact our Client Support Debt Management team about your repayment amount. They'll work with you on a repayment plan based on what you can afford. Phone us When you call, they'll ask you: - your contact details, e.g. address, phone and email - about your income - about your expenses - if you have any dependent children. You may be asked to provide proof.

chunks.title: Setting up debt repayments
chunks.text: We want to help you repay your debt in a way that best suits your situation. We have a range of repayment options available, it depends if you're making payments from New Zealand or overseas. How to repay debt from New Zealand How to repay debt from overseas

chunks.title: While repaying your debt - tell us about any changes
chunks.text: If you have a change in circumstances while repaying your debt, you need to contact our Client Support Debt Management team. Phone us This could be changes for: - your address - your contact details - if you go overseas. If you get a new job, let our Client Support Debt Management team know before you start. Then they can arrange for repayments to be deducted from your wages with your new employer.

chunks.title: If you miss a debt repayment
chunks.text: If you miss a repayment, we'll send you a reminder letter. We don't charge penalties or interest. If you're having trouble repaying your debt, contact our Client Support Debt Management team. They can work with you on a repayment plan that suits you. Phone us

chunks.title: If you don't repay your debt
chunks.text: We understand that it can be hard to stretch your budget to include debt repayments. If you're struggling to repay your debt, contact our Client Support Debt Management team. They can work with you on a repayment plan based on what you can afford. Phone us We won't charge interest or impose penalties on your debt. We'll try to contact you several times about your debt. If you don't respond, we'll seek to get the money back in other ways. To find out your current circumstances, we compare information with other government agencies, e.g. Inland Revenue. There are legal steps we can take which allow us to recover your debt without your consent, such as: - making deductions from your wages, or - making deductions from your bank account.

chunks.title: If you don't repay your debt
chunks.text: If you don't pay back your debt, it could affect what financial help you can get from us in the future.

chunks.text: If you're getting a main benefit, NZ Super, Veteran's Pension or Accommodation Supplement, we'll work with you on a repayment plan that suits you. You can also set up a separate repayment arrangement if you want to. Go to the page 'Your debt with us' if you want information about: - how to get a breakdown of your debt - what to do if you don't agree with your debt - support for managing your debt. Your debt with us

chunks.title: Debt repayment information
chunks.text: If you're not getting a main benefit, NZ Super, Veteran's Pension or Accommodation Supplement, there's a different process for your debt repayments. What we mean by 'main benefit' Repaying debt if you're not getting a benefit or pension

chunks.title: Debt repayment amount
chunks.text: We'll set up a repayment amount depending on your circumstances. We want to make sure this is affordable for you. When deciding how much your repayments should be, you'll need to think of things like: - your budget - your upcoming expenses - any other debts you may have - how long you want to be repaying the money. Call us on 0800 559 009 to: - discuss debt repayments - set up a time to talk to your case manager, if you want to - talk to us about any questions you have about your debt.

chunks.title: Setting up debt repayments
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 to set up debt repayments. We'll set these up so they come out of your benefit, pension or Accommodation Supplement. If you want to pay the debt off faster you can make extra repayments at any time. You can also set up a separate repayment arrangement via internet or telephone banking if you want to. If you're getting a Student Allowance, you need to contact StudyLink. Contact us (Studylink)external

chunks.title: Set up repayment via internet or telephone banking
chunks.text: You can make a one-off payment or set up regular payments using internet or telephone banking. Your bank may charge you for these services. To set up the payments you'll need the account number: 03-0049-0006243-025. If your bank only needs a 2 digit suffix, use 25 instead of 025. Once you enter the account number, your bank may match it to the account name it uses for us. If your bank doesn't match it, you can use the account name 'Work and Income Debt Management'. In the reference field, you need to put the letter 'S', followed by your 9 digit client number.

chunks.title: If your benefit, pension or Accommodation Supplement is about to stop
chunks.text: If you owe us money and your benefit, pension or Accommodation Supplement is about to stop, you need to call us on 0800 559 009 to: - let us know when your payment needs to stop - arrange an exit interview with us where we can discuss your repayment options. You'll be able to pay your debt off either: - in a lump sum, or - each week at an amount you can afford.

chunks.title: If you're going into full-time work
chunks.text: If you’re going into full-time work and can get Assistance to Transition into Employment, you may be able to stop repaying your debt for 3 months. This is called a 3 month debt recovery suspension. This is to help you pay for work related costs. Talk to us at your exit interview about whether you qualify for this payment.

chunks.title: Repaying a previous COVID-19 payment
chunks.text: Find out when you need to repay a previous COVID-19 payment and how to repay it. Businesses could apply for a COVID-19 payment to help to pay their employees, including self-employed people. This includes the COVID-19 Wage Subsidies, the Leave Support Scheme and the Short-Term Absence Payment.

chunks.title: When you need to repay
chunks.text: You need to repay some or all of a COVID-19 payment if you or your employee were not eligible for it during the payment timeframe. This could be because something changed later on. You may have to make a repayment if: - you no longer meet the criteria for the payment - you did not use the payment to keep or pay your staff - you provided false or misleading information in your application - your employee has resigned, been dismissed, or no longer meets the criteria for the payment (you can use the money to pay other affected employees, or repay it) - your employee has been made redundant or their contract finished (you need to repay the remaining amount after you've paid them their wage) - your business has closed

chunks.title: When you need to repay
chunks.text: - you applied for the wrong payment rate (e.g. you applied for a full-time rate when you only need the part-time rate) - you're self-employed and your regular business income is less than the COVID-19 payment (you need to repay the surplus) - you're a state sector organisation who didn't have an exception approved, oryour business got a payment it is not entitled to due to a Ministry of Social Development error.

chunks.title: How to make a repayment
chunks.text: You can make a repayment by filling out our online 'Repayment request' form: You'll need to tell us your: - business name - IRD number - New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), if you have one - phone number - email address - postal address, and - the amount you need to repay. Repayment requestexternal Once we process the form, we'll be in touch to confirm how to make the repayment.
