chunks.title: Winter Energy Payment
chunks.text: The Winter Energy Payment is an extra payment to help with the cost of heating your home over the winter months. You must be getting a main benefit, pension or Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. You don't need to apply for the Winter Energy Payment. If you meet the criteria, it's paid automatically from 1 May to 1 October every year. The Winter Energy Payment starts on 1 May and ends on 1 October every year.

chunks.title: When you get your first payment
chunks.text: 1 May 2026 is a Friday and we pay you for the week that's just been. This means if you get paid weekly, your first payment will be a part-payment in the week of 4 May. You'll get the full amount in the week of 11 May. If you get paid NZ Super or Veteran’s Pension, your first payment will be a part-payment on 5 May. You'll get the full amount on 19 May.

chunks.title: Who can get the Winter Energy Payment
chunks.text: You'll only get the Winter Energy Payment if you get one of these payments from us: - NZ Super - Veteran's Pension - Jobseeker Support - Jobseeker Support Student Hardship - Sole Parent Support - Supported Living Payment - Young Parent Payment - Youth Payment - Emergency Benefit - Emergency Maintenance Allowance. You also cannot be: - getting Residential Care Subsidy or Residential Support Subsidy - living overseas, or - getting an overseas pension which means you don't get any NZ Super or Veteran's Pension.

chunks.title: Winter Energy Payment dates
chunks.text: The Winter Energy Payment is paid from 1 May to 1 October.

chunks.title: Winter Energy Payment rates
chunks.text: Single people with no dependent children $20.46 a week Couples, and people with dependent children $31.82 a week You'll get the Winter Energy Payment automatically, along with your other regular payments from us (either weekly or fortnightly). The Winter Energy Payment: - doesn't affect your other payments from us, or your Income Related Rent - is a non-taxable payment - can't be paid as a lump sum.

chunks.title: Couples getting NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: Couples are paid $31.82, whether you live together or separately. It's paid to one person in the couple. The system we use for payments can't split it to pay into 2 separate accounts. Generally, we'll pay it into the bank account of the person in the couple who has the lowest client number. You can find your client number on your Community Services Card, SuperGold Card or letters from us. If you'd like to switch the payment to the other person's account, please call us. Phone us

chunks.title: Overseas travel when you're getting NZ Super or Veteran's Pension
chunks.text: If you're heading away from New Zealand over the winter months, we can keep paying your Winter Energy Payment for up to 28 days. Tell us if you plan to leave New Zealand for more than 28 days, otherwise we might pay you too much and have to ask for some money back. The easiest way to let us know is to either: - fill out and submit the overseas travel dates online formexternal - call us on our Seniors line, 0800 552 002

chunks.title: When you return to New Zealand
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand: - before 1 October, you need to contact us so we can start your Winter Energy Payment again. Call our Seniors line on 0800 552 002 - after 1 October, your Winter Energy Payment will automatically start again next year, as long as you still qualify.

chunks.title: Overseas travel and getting a benefit
chunks.text: You need to let us know your travel plans, the reasons for travelling, and for how long. Going overseas If you're able to keep getting your benefit when you're overseas, we'll also keep paying your Winter Energy Payment for up to 28 days.

chunks.title: When you return to New Zealand
chunks.text: If you return to New Zealand: - before 1 October, you need to contact us so we can start your Winter Energy Payment again. Call us on 0800 559 009 - after 1 October, your Winter Energy Payment will automatically start again next year, as long as you still qualify.

chunks.title: Opt out of the payment
chunks.text: If you meet the criteria, the Winter Energy Payment is paid automatically from 1 May to 1 October. It's paid with your main benefit, pension or Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. If you do not want the Winter Energy Payment, you can opt out of getting it by either: - completing the 'Stop or restart Winter Energy Payment' form, or - contacting us. Phone us We won't re-start it for you (even in future years) unless you ask us to.

chunks.title: Fill in the form
chunks.text: You can only fill in this form if you meet the criteria for Winter Energy Payment. This means you must be getting a main benefit, pension or Jobseeker Support Student Hardship. If you get Special Benefit or Temporary Additional Support - please call us instead of filling out this form. Phone us You'll need the following information to complete the form: - client number - name and date of birth - email address and contact number. If you have a partner, the payment can only be started or stopped as a couple. The form will ask you to confirm you both agree to this. Stop or restart Winter Energy Payment

chunks.title: If you've opted out, you can opt back in
chunks.text: Once you've opted out, we won't re-start it for you (even in future years) unless you ask us to. If you want to re-start it, you need to fill out the same form, or contact us.

chunks.title: Work Bonus
chunks.text: If you're on a benefit and choose to work even though you don't have work obligations, you may be able to get a Work Bonus.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may be able to get Work Bonus if you're getting either: - Sole Parent Support, and your youngest child is under 3 - Emergency Maintenance Allowance, and your youngest child is under 3 - Supported Living Payment, because you've got a health condition, injury or disability, or - Emergency Benefit instead of Supported Living Payment because you don't have New Zealand residency. You also need to: - be coming off one of these benefits to start work - be starting work in New Zealand - tell us you want to stop your benefit within 14 days of starting work.

chunks.title: Who can't get Work Bonus
chunks.text: You can't get Work Bonus if: - you're coming off your benefit to start self-employed work, or - you have work obligations while you're on your benefit.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: Work Bonus is paid weekly. The first week's payment will be at the full rate of the benefit you're on. This doesn't include any other payments you get, e.g. Accommodation Supplement or Disability Allowance. It then reduces by $100 a week until it runs out. You can only get one Work Bonus a year. It's not counted as income (including for Working for Families Tax Credits) or as an asset.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: Call us on 0800 559 009 to let us know you've found a job. If you qualify for Work Bonus, we'll pay this to you automatically. It will start the week after you get your last benefit payment.

chunks.title: Kōrero Mahi work seminars
chunks.text: At our Kōrero Mahi work seminars you'll get support to get ready to work. We'll explain how we can help you find work, and get you set up to start applying for jobs. Work seminars are in-person seminars held at your local Work and Income office. The seminars take about 1 hour. Narrator [00:00:02]: Here's a bit about what to expect at our Kōrero Mahi work seminars. These seminars are to support you to get ready for work. They are held at your local Work and Income service centre. [Man smiles and raises his hand in a wave. The same man stands in a seminar room next to a 'Work and Income' sign and talks to a group of clients. A presentation slide reads 'Welcome to Kōrero Mahi. Let's talk work'. The text 'Kōrero Mahi - Work Seminars' appears on the screen.

chunks.title: Kōrero Mahi work seminars

A laptop with the 'Kimi Mahi Mai Find a Job' website open appears.] Narrator [00:00:24]: We'll also chat with you one-on-one about what kind of work you can do and what you might need to do to get a job. [Man points into the camera.] Narrator [00:00"42]: If you have to look for or prepare for work to meet your benefit obligations, then you'll need to come to a Kōrero Mahi seminar. chunks.title: Kōrero Mahi work seminars
chunks.text: Man: And just know that we are here to help you along the way. [Man sits at a table in an office. The MSD logo, Work and Income logo and URL 'www.workandincome.govt.nz' appear on the screen.]

chunks.title: Who the seminars are for
chunks.text: You have to go to a seminar if: - you've applied for Jobseeker Support for the first time, and - and you have full-time or part-time work obligations. If you've reapplied for Jobseeker Support at 26 weeks (6 months), you may have to go to a seminar. Find out more on the Reapply for Jobseeker Support page. Reapply for Jobseeker Support You don't have to go if you're getting any other benefit, or if you're getting Jobseeker Support and only have work preparation obligations.

chunks.title: Which seminar you need to go to
chunks.text: If you have full-time work obligations, you need to go to: - 'Kōrero Mahi - Let's talk work' within 2 weeks of starting Jobseeker Support. If you have part-time work obligations, you need to go to: - 'Kōrero Mahi - Into work' within 2 weeks of starting Jobseeker Support. Use the links below to find out what happens at each seminar:

chunks.title: Kōrero Mahi - Let's talk work
chunks.text: You need to go to this seminar if you have full-time work obligations. You need to go within 2 weeks of starting Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: About the seminar
chunks.text: At the seminar we'll tell you about: - what you have to do while you're getting Jobseeker Support - how we can help you get ready for work - where to look for jobs and what help you can get. We'll also talk with you one-on-one about: - what you've been doing to find work - what kind of work you can do - what support you need to get a job, like a CV, training, work gear or clothes - what your next step is to get into work.

chunks.title: Booking a seminar
chunks.text: We'll book you in for a seminar after you apply for Jobseeker Support. We'll do this when you come to your first appointment.

chunks.title: If you can't make it to your seminar
chunks.text: You can rebook in MyMSD if it's the first time you can't make it. Just open your appointment from the home screen and select 'I can't make it'. You can rebook for a date up to 4 weeks in the future. If you can't use MyMSD, call us on 0800 559 009. MyMSDexternal If you can't make it a second time, let us know as soon as possible by calling 0800 559 009. If you have a good reason, we can rebook you again for another date.

chunks.title: Kōrero Mahi - Into work
chunks.text: You need to go to this seminar if you have part-time work obligations because of your health condition or disability. You need to go within 2 weeks of starting Jobseeker Support.

chunks.title: About the seminar
chunks.text: This seminar is to help you prepare and find work that's suitable for you. We want to understand how you're doing and how we can help you. At the seminar we'll talk about: - how we'll work with you - what support we can offer - getting yourself ready to work, finding jobs and ongoing support while you're working - what you have to do while you're getting Jobseeker Support. We'll also talk with you one-on-one about: - your individual situation, so we can understand what's important to you - what kind of work you can do - what we can do to help you find the right job. Seminars are held in a private room at your local Work and Income office, with a small group of people. We won't discuss your personal situation in a group setting.

chunks.title: Booking a Kōrero Mahi - Into work seminar
chunks.text: You need to come to a seminar within 2 weeks of starting Jobseeker Support. We'll book the seminar for you, and let you know when and where it is.

chunks.title: If you can't make it to your seminar
chunks.text: You can rebook in MyMSD if it's the first time you can't make it. Just open your appointment from the home screen and select 'I can't make it'. You can rebook for a date up to 4 weeks in the future. If you can't use MyMSD, call us on 0800 559 009. MyMSDexternal If you can't make it a second time, let us know as soon as possible by calling 0800 559 009. If you have a good reason, we can rebook you again for another date.

chunks.title: After your seminar
chunks.text: By the end of the seminar you'll know what you need to do to get yourself ready to work, and where to look for jobs. If there’s something you need specific help with that we talked about at your seminar, we’ll be in touch to sort this out. These things can also help: - Get ready to work – specialised help with CVs, cover letters, or job interviews. - Feeling anxious about work – talk to someone if you need support or you’re feeling anxious. - Find jobs – places you can look for jobs and find the right job for you. - Where to look for jobs – job-search websites where you can find something that works for you. - How to choose the right job – tools and experts to help you find out what you're good at and what job suits you.

chunks.title: What happens if you don't go to the seminar
chunks.text: Attending the 'Kōrero Mahi - Let's talk work' and 'Kōrero Mahi - Into work' seminars is part of your obligations to look for or prepare for work. If you don't attend (and you haven’t rebooked), you need to have a good reason why you couldn't come. Otherwise your Jobseeker Support could reduce or stop.

chunks.title: Work, training and study arrangements
chunks.text: If the number of hours that you or your partner work, train or study each week changes, you must tell us as soon as possible as it could affect how much we pay for your childcare.

chunks.title: How to tell us
chunks.text: You need to complete a change in circumstances form for each child. You can complete the form online and print it. - View or download Childcare Assistance - Change of circumstances form. - Get your childcare provider to sign the form. - If you or your partner are studying, your education provider will also need to sign it. - Post the signed form to us with supporting documents (the Change of Circumstances form will tell you what you'll need to provide) to your local service centre, or drop off at one of our service centres. If you can't print the form, contact us on 0800 559 009 and we'll send one to you. Find your nearest service centre

chunks.title: Working for Families
chunks.text: Working for Families is help from Work and Income and Inland Revenue (IR) to make it easier to work and raise a family.

chunks.title: What Work and Income help with
chunks.text: Work and Income help with: - childcare costs for pre-school care - childcare costs for before and after school care - accommodation costs with the Accommodation Supplement You can use our 'Check what you might get' tool to find out what Work and Income payments you might qualify for and how much you might be able to get. Childcare Subsidy Out of School Care and Recreation (OSCAR) Subsidy Accommodation Supplement

chunks.title: What Inland Revenue help with
chunks.text: Inland Revenue (IR) can help you with Working for Families Tax Credits. Apply for Working for Families (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: Family tax credit
chunks.text: This payment provides ongoing financial support for families. The amount you receive depends on your family situation. If you're on a Work and Income benefit you can get us to pay your family tax credit with your other payments. Inland Revenue pay the family tax credit to you if you're not getting a benefit payment from us. Family tax credit (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: Best Start tax credit
chunks.text: Best Start tax credit (BSTC) is a payment to help families with the costs in a child's first three years. If you're getting a Work and Income benefit, we'll pay you the Best Start tax credit with your payments. You'll need to apply through IR if you don't get a benefit from Work and Income. Best Start (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: In-work tax credit
chunks.text: In-work tax credit (IWTC) is an entitlement from Inland Revenue for people in paid work with families. In-work tax credit (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: Minimum family tax credit
chunks.text: Minimum family tax credit (MFTC) is a payment made by Inland Revenue to families with dependent children, so there is a minimum income each week after tax. Minimum family tax credit (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: Work out your tax credits
chunks.text: Working for Families payments are based on your family income and the number of children in your care. Use Inland Revenue's calculator to estimate how much your Working for Families payments could be. Can you get Working for Families? (Inland Revenue)external

chunks.title: Worried about losing your job
chunks.text: If you're struggling at work or worried you might lose your job, we can help. Tell us what's going on and we'll create a tailored plan to help you. Things don't always go to plan, but that's OK. We have a dedicated team who can help you keep your job or find a new one. We can help if: - you're worried you might lose your job, for any reason - you're struggling to do your job - you're finding work hard - your contract is about to end. Contact us early so we can help you right away, even if no decisions have been made yet. We'll do our best to help you keep your current job. If that's not possible, we'll help you get a new job as soon as possible.

chunks.title: How we can help
chunks.text: We may be able to help you and your employer to avoid making your job redundant. Talk to us as early as possible, even if you're not sure if you'll lose your job. We'll talk about your situation right now, and how we can help. We can do things like: - check how we can help your employer keep your job going - figure out what your options are and talk through these with you - find training options that can help you do your job - help you upskill into a new job. You don't have to be getting a benefit for this. If you've already lost your job, or it's about to finish, we can still help. We'll help you get a new job as soon as possible, and support you between jobs: Redundancy support

chunks.title: How to contact us
chunks.text: Email our team at RedeploymentSupport@msd.govt.nz In your email tell us: - your name - your contact details - how your job is going and what's worrying you. We'll connect you to someone in your area who will talk to you directly to understand what's going on and what you need.

chunks.title: Help for your job
chunks.text: As well as talking to us, there are also other things we can do to help you with your current job.

chunks.title: Feeling anxious about work
chunks.text: It can be hard to do your job if you're worried or anxious about work. These services are specifically designed to help people with their jobs, or help them get a job: Feeling anxious about work

chunks.title: Seasonal work
chunks.text: If your seasonal job is finishing soon, we can help you get set to find a new one. Finished seasonal work

chunks.title: Costs while you're working
chunks.text: We may be able to help you pay an unexpected cost, or pay your bills, even if you've got a job. Help while you’re working

chunks.title: Paying for work costs
chunks.text: Get help from us to pay for things you need to do your job like training, transport, gear or clothing. Payments to help you at work

chunks.title: Young Parent Payment
chunks.text: Young Parent Payment helps young parents aged 16-19 year olds.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may get the Young Parent Payment if you: - are 16-19 years old - have a dependent child or children - are a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident - normally live in New Zealand and intend to stay here. You must also: - be in, or available for, full time education, training or work-based learning leading towards an NCEA level 2 qualification, or an equivalent or higher qualification - be in a teen parent unit if your child is one year old, or from six months old if there is a place available for you - work with a Youth Service provider who will help you manage your money - attend a budgeting course - attend a parenting course to develop your parenting skills - enrol your child (or children) at a medical centre or with a doctor

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: - register your children under 5 with a WellChild provider, like Plunket, and make sure they have regular checkups with this provider - have your child (or children) attend Early Childhood Education or other suitable childcare when you are in education, training or work-based learning or part-time work.

chunks.title: You're single
chunks.text: If you're single and 16 or 17, you may only get Young Parent Payment if you either: - have a parental support gap - are living at home with, or being financially supported by, your parents or guardians and they earn less than the Family Tax Credit income cut-off point, or - are divorced, your civil union has been dissolved, or you have separated from your de-facto partner. You are considered to have a parental support gap if either: - you have left the care of Oranga Tamariki - Ministry for Children, or - your parents or guardian can't support you. This could be because they are in prison, in hospital, deceased, or overseas, or - your relationship with your parents or guardians has broken down and no one can support you financially, or

chunks.title: You're single
chunks.text: - there is a good reason why you can no longer live with your parents or guardian, or be supported by them or anyone else. You would not be considered to have a parental support gap if you have the option of living with a parent or guardian but choose not to without a good and sufficient reason.

chunks.title: You're in a relationship
chunks.text: If you're married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, you may get Young Parent Payment as long as you're not in a relationship with a specified beneficiary If you or your partner are 16 or 17, a Family Court Judge must consent to your relationship. You'll need to show us the court order from the Family Court Judge. Before 14 August 2018, we accepted written consent from the parents of the 16-17 year old. If you've already given the parents' consent to us before then, we can still use it. You don't need to get consent from a Family Court Judge.

chunks.title: Check if you can get Young Parent Payment
chunks.text: To find out if you could get Young Parent Payment and what else you might qualify for, use our 'Check what you might get' tool.

chunks.title: What you can get
chunks.text: How much you get depends on your situation. Current rates (Map)external

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You can apply online through MyMSD. We'll also check to see if you can get any other help from us based on the answers you give in your application. If you want to get child support through Inland Revenue, you can apply through us when you complete your online application. Or you can apply through Inland Revenue. Any child support payments you get will be counted as income for your benefit. Child Support

chunks.title: What happens next
chunks.text: Once you've submitted your online form, we'll call if there's anything else you need to do.

chunks.title: Parent/caregiver involvement
chunks.text: When you apply for a Young Parent Payment, we usually discuss your situation with your parents or caregivers. There are some circumstances when this won't happen, for example, if you're married or in a civil union. Information for parents/caregivers

chunks.title: Education and Training
chunks.text: Most young people are better off if they finish their education or are in training for future work. When you apply, we'll call you to talk about what education or training you'll return to, start or continue doing.

chunks.title: Your rights at work and advice
chunks.text: Work can be a stressful place, and sometimes things don't go to plan. You can get help to make your job easier, understand your rights and resolve problems at work.

chunks.title: Feeling anxious
chunks.text: It can be hard to do your job if you're feeling worried or anxious. These coaching and mental health services are designed to help you keep your job or find a new one: Feeling anxious about work

chunks.title: Need training or extra costs to do your job
chunks.text: We may be able to help if you're disabled or have a health condition and need training or have extra costs to do your job. Job and Training Support Funds

chunks.title: Managing challenges at work
chunks.text: If you've come off your benefit for this job, you can get ongoing support and advice to help you manage any challenges. This is called In-Work Support. In-Work Support

chunks.title: Leave and holidays
chunks.text: Employment New Zealand has information about the types of leave you can get and what you need to do to get this. Leave and holidays - Employment New Zealandexternal

chunks.title: How to talk to your employer
chunks.text: Employment New Zealand has advice on the best ways to prevent and resolve relationship problems between you and your employer. Resolving problems - Employment New Zealandexternal

chunks.title: Worried about losing your job
chunks.text: If you're struggling at work or worried you might lose your job, we can help. Tell us what's going on and we'll create a tailored plan to help you keep your job or find a new one. Worried about losing your job

chunks.title: Youth Payment
chunks.text: Youth Payment helps young people aged 16 or 17 who can't live with their parents or guardian and aren't supported by them or anyone else.

chunks.title: Who can get it
chunks.text: You may get Youth Payment if you: - are 16 or 17 - have no dependent children - are a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident - normally live in New Zealand and intend to stay here. You must also: - be in, or available for either: full time education training work-based learning leading towards an NCEA level 2 qualification, or an equivalent or higher qualification - full time education - training - work-based learning leading towards an NCEA level 2 qualification, or an equivalent or higher qualification - work with a Youth Service provider who will help you manage your money - attend a budgeting course.

chunks.title: You're single
chunks.text: If you're single, you may get Youth Payment if you: - have a parental support gap, or - are divorced, or your civil union has been dissolved or you have separated from your de-facto partner.

chunks.title: You're in a relationship
chunks.text: If you're married, in a civil union or de facto relationship, you may get Youth Payment as long as you're not in a relationship with a specified beneficiary. Specified beneficiary A Family Court Judge must consent to your relationship. You'll need to show us the court order from the Family Court Judge. Before 14 August 2018, we accepted written consent from the parents of the 16-17 year old. If you've already given the parents' consent to us before then, we can still use it. You don't need to get consent from a Family Court Judge.

chunks.title: Parental support gap
chunks.text: You are considered to have a parental support gap if: - you have left the care of Oranga Tamariki - Ministry for Children, or - your parents or guardian can't support you. This could be because they are in prison, in hospital, deceased, or overseas, or - your relationship with your parents or guardians has broken down and no one can support you financially, or - there is a good reason why you can no longer live with your parents or guardian, or be supported by them or anyone else. You would not be considered to have a parental support gap if you have the option of living with a parent or guardian but choose not to without a good and sufficient reason.

chunks.title: Parent/caregiver involvement
chunks.text: When you apply for a Youth Payment we usually discuss your situation with your parents or caregivers. There are some circumstances when this won't happen, eg if you are married or in a civil union.

chunks.title: Education & Training
chunks.text: Most young people are better off if they finish their education or are in training for future work. When you apply, we'll call you to talk about what education or training you'll return to, start or continue doing.

chunks.title: How much you can get
chunks.text: This depends on your current circumstances. Current rates (Manuals and Procedures)external When you get Youth Payment we'll automatically pay you the Winter Energy Payment for heating your home over the winter months. Winter Energy Payment

chunks.title: Are you eligible?
chunks.text: Find out if you might get this benefit, and what other financial assistance may be available to you.

chunks.title: How to apply
chunks.text: You can apply online through MyMSD. We'll check to see if you can get any other help from us based on the answers you give in your application. Apply online

chunks.title: What you need to do when you're on a benefit
chunks.text: If you get a benefit from us, you need to keep us up-to-date with any changes that might affect what you're entitled to or how much you get paid. Changes when you're getting a benefit or payment

chunks.title: Do you need to declare income?
chunks.text: If you get a benefit or payment from us you probably have to tell us if you get any extra income. But it depends on the benefits you get. Declare income

chunks.title: Estimate how much will be deducted from your benefit
chunks.text: You can estimate how much will be deducted from your payment if you earn wages while receiving a benefit from us. Income deduction tables
